2.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

3.meaning: they become / come to be — a verb of being or becoming, expressing that a group comes into a certain state.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), marked by the ya- prefix with the plural -ū ending (the closing alif is silent). The short ending (-ū rather than -ūna) shows it has been cut by a preceding particle of negation, condition, or purpose, so it reads 'that they be / they would be / they do not become' depending on that particle.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

4.meaning: Ones who frustrate or escape — those who render another powerless, who thwart, outstrip, or get away beyond reach. 'muʿjizīn' names people who cause incapacity in another, i.e. who escape or cannot be overcome.

parts.en: one who frustrates / escapes (Form IV doer)

4.grammar: An active participle (a noun naming the doer) in the Form IV pattern, 'ones who render [another] unable / who escape'. The '-īna' ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the case used for objects of verbs, after prepositions, and after certain particles. So it denotes 'those who frustrate/escape' as the object or governed term.
4.root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z) — to be unable, powerless; (Form IV) to render unable, frustrate

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
7.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

8.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

8.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
11.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
11.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
14.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

15.meaning: It is multiplied / doubled, increased manifold. From 'ḍāʿafa', to multiply or increase something several times over. In the passive it means 'it is multiplied / increased manyfold'.
15.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the passive voice, so the subject receives the action ('it is multiplied/doubled'). The vowel pattern (yu-...-a-) marks the passive. The 'ya-/yu-' prefix is third-person masculine singular ('it/he'), and the final '-u' ending is indicative, the mood used for a plain factual statement.
15.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to double, multiply, increase manifold

16.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
16.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

17.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
17.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.

18.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
18.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

19.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
19.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

20.meaning: They are able / they have the power and capacity — to be capable of doing something, to have the strength, means, or ability to carry it out.
20.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the present tense and the 'they' subject; the -ūna ending marks the plural and the indicative mood — the plain factual form for an ongoing state. From form X, which often carries the sense of 'seeking/having the capacity for' something, here simply 'to be able.'
20.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, to be capable, willing capacity

21.meaning: The hearing — the faculty or sense of hearing, the capacity by which sound is perceived, made definite by 'the.'
21.grammar: A noun with the prefix al- ('the'); its l assimilates into the following 's' (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced as-samʿ. The final -a marks the accusative, the case for the object of a verb. It denotes the sense of hearing as a definite, known thing.

22.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
22.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

23.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
23.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
23.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

24.meaning: To see, perceive with the eyes, or have insight — to look and take in, with a nuance of clear perception and understanding, not mere glancing. Used of a group: 'they see / perceive'.
24.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they see'). The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action done by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna ending is the 'indicative' form used when the verb is not preceded by something that would shorten it.

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They lost', 'they have suffered loss', 'they ruined themselves' — said of a group of males who have come out as losers, forfeiting or wasting something of value, especially their own selves.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (more than one male) and the action is presented as completed: 'they lost'.
3.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, to lose, to suffer ruin

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
4.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

5.meaning: "And it went astray / was lost / went to ruin." A past-tense verb meaning that something strayed from the right path, missed its target, or vanished and came to nothing. The opening wa- adds "and."
5.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb in the "he/it" third-person masculine singular form. With no subject pronoun attached, the bare verb itself carries the sense "he/it strayed."
5.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, be lost, err

6.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
6.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

7.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
7.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
7.root: — (particle; no root)

8.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
8.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: Part of a fixed expression 'lā jarama' meaning 'no doubt / assuredly / it is inevitable that'. The word 'jarama' here conveys necessity or certainty — that something is bound to be true or earned without escape.

parts.en: fixed final vowel (3rd person masculine singular / built-in ending)

2.grammar: Originally a past-tense verb ('it was earned/made binding'), now used in the frozen expression 'lā jarama' to mean 'no doubt / assuredly / inevitably'. The final '-a' is the third-person masculine singular ending of that old verb form, but in this set phrase the whole functions as an affirmation of certainty rather than an ordinary verb.
2.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to earn, commit, make binding; (root sense) to cut, acquire

3.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
3.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
5.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
5.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

6.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
6.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

7.meaning: An elative/superlative meaning 'the ones who lose the most' or 'the biggest losers' — those whose loss is most ruinous, in the sense of having traded away or wasted what is of true value and ending in ruin.
7.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural noun. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word is the doer or the thing being described. 'akhsar' is the elative pattern 'afʿal' meaning 'most/greater in losing'.
7.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, to lose or suffer ruin

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: 'And they humbled themselves / became lowly and submissive' — to lower oneself before Allah in humility, calm, and reverent obedience.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV, 'afʿala') with the -ū ending meaning 'they' (masculine plural) completed the action. The 'a-' shape of the stem belongs to a derived verb pattern that here carries the sense of entering into a state of humble submission.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
8.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

9.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
9.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

10.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
10.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

11.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
11.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
11.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

12.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
12.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

13.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
13.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

14.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
14.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
14.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: A likeness, comparison, parable, or illustrative example; a similitude used to make something abstract vivid and understandable.
1.grammar: A singular noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described. Being without tanwīn here, it commonly stands as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the likeness OF …').
1.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; likeness, similitude, example

2.meaning: 'the two groups / the two parties' — two distinct camps or factions, named as a pair.
2.grammar: A noun 'group/party' with the definite article al-. The -ayni ending is the dual ('two of them') in its oblique form — the shape a dual noun takes as an object or after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship.
2.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a group split off

3.meaning: 'Like the blind one' — a comparison to a person who cannot see.
3.grammar: The prefix 'ka-' is a particle of comparison meaning 'like' or 'as'. It attaches to the definite noun 'al-aʿmā' ('the blind'), which is on the 'afʿal' pattern used for colours and bodily defects. The word ends in a fixed long 'ā' (alif maqṣūra) and does not change its ending for case.

4.meaning: 'And the deaf one' — a person who cannot hear.
4.grammar: A definite noun on the 'afʿal' pattern (used for defects). The -i ending is genitive: it typically appears when the word follows a preposition or comparison particle, or links to a preceding noun. The doubled final 'm' (shadda) is part of the root, which has a repeated consonant.

5.meaning: 'And the one who sees' — a seeing, sighted person; one possessing clear vision or insight.
5.grammar: A definite noun on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, denoting one who possesses the quality fully ('seeing'). The -i ending is genitive, the case used after prepositions or when the word is linked to a preceding noun.
5.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, seeing, perception

6.meaning: 'And the one who hears' — a hearing person; one who hears and perceives.
6.grammar: A definite noun on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern ('hearing'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 's' (a 'sun letter'), shown by the doubling. The -i ending is genitive, used after prepositions or linking to a preceding noun.

7.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
7.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

8.meaning: 'The two of them are equal / are alike' — two things being on the same level, matching one another.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb (form VIII, 'iftaʿala') meaning 'to be/become equal'. The 'ya-' prefix marks third person, and the '-āni' ending is the dual, meaning 'the two of them' do the action. The retained final 'ni' shows the verb is in its base (indicative) state.

9.meaning: 'A likeness / example / parable / comparison.' A noun denoting something put forward as an illustration or analogy — a similitude that clarifies a point by comparison. It can also mean a proverb or a model case.
9.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon); the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an example / some likeness').
9.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, to resemble; example, model

10.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
10.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

11.meaning: 'You take heed / become mindful / receive a reminder' — to reflect, remember, and let oneself be admonished and reminded of the truth.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb (form V, 'tafaʿʿala', reflexive). The 'ta-' prefix plus the '-ūna' ending means 'you (plural) do this'. The retained 'na' marks the indicative (base) mood. The doubled middle consonant is the form-V pattern, giving the sense of taking a reminder to heart. (Originally tatadhakkarūna, with one 'ta' dropped.)
11.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembrance, recollection, reminder

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

3.meaning: Nūḥ (Noah), the proper name of the early prophet; in the form that marks him as the object of a verb.
3.grammar: A proper name in the accusative case, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb. As a foreign proper name, Nūḥ is normally diptote (ghayr munṣarif) and would take a bare -a without nunation; the nunated -an form (nūḥan) is exceptional and is explained by grammarians as making the name fully declinable on account of its lightness (three letters with a quiescent middle), an option permitted for such short names.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
4.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

5.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, kinsfolk, or nation to which someone belongs.
5.grammar: A noun ('people') with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his') making it possessive. The -i case ending is genitive — both because the word is owned/linked and because the 'hi' form of the pronoun follows it. 'qawm' refers to a collective body of people.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group / community

6.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
6.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

7.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

8.meaning: A warner — one who gives warning, alerting people to impending danger or consequence so they may take heed. It names the agent who delivers such an admonition.
8.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive agent-pattern (faʿīl), denoting one who does something fully or by office — a 'warner'. The ending -un is nominative and indefinite ('a warner'); the nominative marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate, so this typically stands as 'is a warner' or 'a warner (came)'.
8.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of danger

9.meaning: Clear, plain, and self-evident; that which makes things manifest. The form carries an active sense: not merely 'clear in itself' but 'making clear,' something that openly displays its nature and leaves no ambiguity.
9.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) on the form mufʿil, meaning 'one who/that which makes [something] clear.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
1.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

2.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
2.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

3.meaning: (That) you should serve and worship — to direct devotion, obedience, and humble submission to one worthy of it; the act of ʻībāda (worship) addressed to a group.
3.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb. The ta- prefix marks a 'you' subject, and the -ū ending makes it plural ('you all'). When governed by a preceding particle the form takes the subjunctive ('that you may worship'); the dropped final nūn (written ū rather than ūna) reflects that subjunctive/jussive state.

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
5.root: — (proper name)

6.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
6.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

7.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').
7.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, fright, awe

8.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
8.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

9.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

10.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
10.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

11.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
11.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.
11.root: ا-ل-م (ʾ-l-m) — pain, to feel pain

1.meaning: 'Then he said / so he said' — the past-tense verb 'he said,' introduced by a connector meaning 'then / so,' marking what follows as the next or resulting step.
1.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' linking this to what came before and often implying sequence or consequence. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the base vowel of the 3rd-person masculine singular past form, marking that a single masculine subject performed the action.

2.meaning: The chiefs, leading men, or notables — the prominent council of a people; a collective term for the elite whose standing fills the eyes.
2.grammar: A definite noun (the al- prefix means 'the') with the -u (nominative) ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence — the ones doing or being something. Though singular in form, it refers collectively to the leading body of a people.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
6.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: 'We see you' — to perceive or regard you, whether with the eyes or in the sense of considering/judging you to be a certain way.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb from a 'weak' root whose final letter drops. The 'na-' prefix means 'we', and the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (one male). Together: 'we see / we regard you'.
8.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving, forming an opinion

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: 'A human being / a mortal man' — a member of humankind, emphasising ordinary flesh-and-blood humanity as opposed to something angelic or divine.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative case (the object or the thing being described/named) and the absence of 'the' ('a human being'). 'bashar' denotes humankind with stress on bodily, mortal nature.
10.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — human skin; humankind, mortal nature

11.meaning: 'Like us / similar to us' — of the same kind or equal in nature to us.
11.grammar: The noun 'mithl' ('a like, an equal') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The -a ending is accusative, the case for an object or descriptive complement. With the pronoun it means 'one like us'.
11.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, resemblance

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: 'We see you' — to perceive or regard you, whether with the eyes or in the sense of considering/judging you to be a certain way.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb from a 'weak' root whose final letter drops. The 'na-' prefix means 'we', and the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (one male). Together: 'we see / we regard you'.
13.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving, forming an opinion

14.meaning: 'Followed you / went after you' — to follow behind, adhere to, and take as one's lead or example.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb (form VIII) in the third-person masculine singular: 'he followed.' The -a ending marks completed past action by a single male doer, and the attached -ka ('you,' masculine singular) is the object — the one who is followed.
14.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

16.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
16.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

17.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
17.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

18.meaning: 'Our lowliest ones / the basest among us' — those regarded as the meanest, most contemptible, or lowest in social standing of a group.
18.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'the lowest/basest ones', with attached '-nā' ('our'). The -u ending is nominative, the case used when the word is the subject or what is being predicated. The plural pattern 'afāʿil' here marks the lowest-ranking members of a group.
18.root: ر-ذ-ل (r-dh-l) — baseness, vileness, being low or despised

19.meaning: 'Outwardly / at first glance / on the surface' (in the sense of immature, superficial judgement); literally 'apparent, manifest'. It describes something taken at its first, surface appearance.
19.grammar: An active participle ('one that appears/is apparent') on the 'fāʿil' pattern, from a weak-final root. The -a ending is accusative, the case used for an adverbial sense such as 'at first/superficially' or for an object. It conveys the surface, outward aspect of a thing.
19.root: ب-د-و (b-d-w) — to appear, become visible, emerge into view

20.meaning: 'The opinion / the view / the judgement' — the faculty or act of forming a considered opinion or seeing a matter in one's mind.
20.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the opinion/view'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), shown by the doubling. The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or when the word is linked to a preceding noun (as a possessive/'of' relation).
20.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving, opinion / considered view

21.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
21.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

22.meaning: We see, perceive, behold, or observe; to take in with the eye, and by extension to know or witness. Carries a sense of attentive regard.
22.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 1st person plural ('we'). The na- prefix marks the 'we' doer. This is a 'defective' verb with a weak third root letter, so it ends in a long -ā. In the indicative (the plain factual 'we do/are doing' sense) this ending stays as -ā.

23.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
23.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

24.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
24.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

26.meaning: Bounty, grace, favor; an overflowing generosity or surplus given freely. It denotes goodness and abundance bestowed beyond what is owed or expected, and by extension excellence or superiority.
26.grammar: The -in ending is genitive plus 'tanwīn' (the -n indicating indefiniteness, 'a bounty'). The genitive case typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF bounty') or follows a preposition.
26.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — bounty, grace, excess goodness, superiority

27.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
27.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

28.meaning: 'We think you / we consider you' (to be such-and-such) — to suppose, reckon, or be of the opinion that you are in a certain state.
28.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'na-' prefix ('we') and attached object '-kum' ('you', plural). The '-u' before the pronoun marks the indicative (base) mood. 'ẓann' means to hold an opinion or strong supposition that falls short of certainty.

29.meaning: 'Liars / ones who lie' — people characterised by speaking falsehood.
29.grammar: An active participle ('one who lies') on the 'fāʿil' pattern, in the sound masculine plural. The '-īna' ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case — the form used when the word is an object or otherwise not the subject.
29.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — lying, falsehood, denying the truth

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
2.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

3.meaning: 'Have you considered? / Tell me / What do you think?' — a set rhetorical opening that calls the listener to reflect: literally 'have you (all) seen?'
3.grammar: A past-tense verb of perception with the subject suffix '-tum' ('you', plural), opened by the question particle 'a-' ('do/have…?'). Idiomatically it means 'tell me / what is your view?', summoning the listener to consider a matter.

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'I was / I had been,' the core verb of being placed in the past for the speaker. It links 'I' to a past state or description: 'I used to be / I came to be in such a condition.'
5.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular. The suffix '-tu' is the past-tense ending that means 'I' (the one who did/was). It expresses a completed or settled past state — 'I was, I had been.'
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

7.meaning: A clear proof, plain sign, or self-evident demonstration; something that makes the truth manifest and removes doubt.
7.grammar: A noun (also usable as an intensive adjective) meaning a clear, evident proof. The -in ending is indefinite and genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… of …"), follows a preposition, or follows a quantity word.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, to make plain, distinguish

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: 'My Lord' — the word 'rabb' denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, governs and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached 'my' it expresses one's own Lord and Caretaker.
9.grammar: A noun followed by the possessive ending '-ī' meaning 'my', which joins to the noun and also serves the genitive (possessive) relationship. The attached '-ī' both makes the noun definite and shows ownership: 'my Lord'.

10.meaning: 'And He has given me / granted me' — the bestowal of something upon the speaker by another (the giver being a single 'He').
10.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV, 'ātā', 'to give/bestow') from a weak-final root. It carries a third-person singular 'he' subject, and the attached '-nī' ('me') is the object — 'he gave me'. The linking 'n' (nūn al-wiqāya) protects the verb's ending before the 'me' pronoun.
10.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring/give, bestow

11.meaning: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
11.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.
11.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

13.meaning: His presence, His keeping, that which is 'with' Him or proceeds from Him. 'ʿind' denotes being at, near, or in the possession of someone; with the 'His' pronoun it points to what lies in Allah's own keeping or comes from Him.
13.grammar: An adverb of place ('with, in the presence of') joined to the possessive pronoun -hi ('his/him'). The -i vowel before the pronoun reflects the genitive state — the form this word takes after a preposition or when bound to what precedes it; -hi names the one in whose presence something is.
13.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or in the keeping of

14.meaning: 'So/then it was made obscure / hidden / unclear to (someone)' — something rendered blind or concealed so that one cannot perceive it.
14.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (form II, 'fuʿʿila'), so the doer is unnamed — 'it was made obscure'. The '-at' ending marks a feminine singular subject ('it/she'). The prefix 'fa-' means 'so/then'. The doubled middle consonant and the 'u-…-i' vowels are the passive of the intensive form.

15.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
15.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

16.meaning: 'Shall we compel / oblige you to (accept) it?' — a question about forcing something upon a group as a binding obligation.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV, 'alzama', 'to oblige/compel') opened by the question particle 'a-' ('shall…?'). The 'nu-' prefix means 'we'. It carries two attached objects: '-kumū' ('you', plural) and '-hā' ('it'). The 'u' in '-kumū' is a connecting vowel between the two pronouns.
16.root: ل-ز-م (l-z-m) — to cling, be binding; (form IV) to impose, oblige

17.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
17.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

18.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
18.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

19.meaning: An active participle (a doer-noun) meaning 'ones who dislike / are averse / find something hateful' — people who feel reluctance or aversion toward something.
19.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural, naming those who carry out the action: 'those who dislike'. The -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the nominative case, which is typically used for the subject or for a predicate describing the subject.
19.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — to dislike, be averse, find hateful

1.meaning: 'And O my people!' — an affectionate call addressed to one's own community or kinsfolk.
1.grammar: A direct address: 'wa' ('and') plus the vocative particle 'yā' ('O') calling 'qawm' ('people'). The final -i stands in for the possessive 'my' (the 'ī' is shortened/dropped), so it means 'O my people'. 'qawm' is a collective term for one's community.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group / community

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: 'I ask you (for)…'. A present-tense verb 'I ask/request', with the object pronoun 'you' (plural) attached. Used of asking a question or requesting something such as payment or reward.
3.grammar: The a- prefix marks a first-person singular present-tense verb: 'I ask'. The attached -kum is the object 'you (plural)'. The underlying final vowel on the verb is -u (indicative, the ordinary present-tense mood), here followed directly by the object pronoun.

4.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
4.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

5.meaning: 'Wealth / property / possessions' — material goods, money, and assets that a person owns.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative case (the object of a verb or otherwise governed) together with the absence of 'the' ('wealth / some property'). 'māl' covers money, property, and possessions generally.
5.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, to be wealthy

6.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
6.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

7.meaning: My reward, my wage, my recompense — the payment or return that is due specifically to the speaker for what they have done.
7.grammar: A singular noun with the attached pronoun '-iya' ('my'). When the possessive '-ī/-iya' is joined, it stands in place of the usual case-vowel, so the noun reads simply as 'my reward', the thing belonging to the speaker.
7.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for effort

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

9.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
9.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
9.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
11.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

12.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
12.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

13.meaning: 'One who drives away / repels / chases off' — someone who expels or turns others away.
13.grammar: An active participle ('one who drives away') on the 'fāʿil' pattern, preceded by the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with/by'). Here 'bi-' is the emphatic bi- (bi' al-tawkīd): attached to a nominal predicate that falls under a negation, it strengthens that negation (giving the force 'by no means / not at all a driver-away'). It does not signal future time; the negation comes from the surrounding context, not from 'bi-' itself. The -i ending is genitive, the case governed by 'bi-'.
13.root: ط-ر-د (ṭ-r-d) — to drive off, expel, chase away

14.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
14.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
15.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

16.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
16.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

17.meaning: 'Ones who meet / will meet' — those who encounter or come face to face with someone. Built on a form meaning a mutual meeting or encounter.
17.grammar: An active participle, 'ones who meet/encounter' (the 'mu-' prefix forms a doer). It is a masculine sound plural; the '-ū' ending here is the plural-subject form with its final 'n' dropped because it stands in an 'of'-construction directly before the following noun.
17.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

18.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
18.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
18.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

19.meaning: "And yet I… / But as for me…" — a compound joining the conjunction 'and' to the contrastive particle 'but/however' (which corrects or counters a preceding statement), ending in an attached 'I'. It strongly draws attention to the speaker's own contrasting position.
19.grammar: A conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lākinna, a particle of correction that contradicts what came before. Like inna, lākinna governs the following noun or pronoun in the accusative (naṣb) and places emphasis on it; the doubled 'n' carries that emphasis. The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun, here in its accusative position as the noun of lākinna, so the whole reads an emphatic 'and yet as for me'.

20.meaning: A past-tense verb from the root of seeing, in the causative sense 'he showed / let you see / made you behold' something. So: 'he caused you (plural) to see'.
20.grammar: A perfect (past) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative (Form IV) pattern ('to make someone see' = to show). The final long vowel of the stem is a weak (defective) root letter. The attached -kum is the object 'you all'.
20.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see; (causative) to show, cause to behold

21.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
21.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
21.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

22.meaning: You act ignorantly; you behave foolishly without knowledge. The verb conveys being or acting in ignorance — lacking knowledge and behaving rashly because of it.
22.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb. The ta- prefix here marks a second-person addressee, and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'you (all)' in the indicative mood, indicating a real, ongoing action. The full -ūna (not shortened to -ū) shows the verb stands free of any particle that would cut it short.

1.meaning: 'And O my people!' — an affectionate call addressed to one's own community or kinsfolk.
1.grammar: A direct address: 'wa' ('and') plus the vocative particle 'yā' ('O') calling 'qawm' ('people'). The final -i stands in for the possessive 'my' (the 'ī' is shortened/dropped), so it means 'O my people'. 'qawm' is a collective term for one's community.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group / community

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: "He helps/supports me" — to come to someone's aid, grant victory, defend or back them against an adversary, with an attached 'me' as the one being helped.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb: the ya- prefix marks 'he' as the doer and the -u ending marks the plain present/future indicative ('helps / will help'). The attached -nī is the object pronoun 'me', with its protective 'n' (nūn al-wiqāya) linking verb to pronoun.

4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
6.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

7.meaning: "I drove them away / repelled them" — to push or chase someone off, expel or banish them, with an attached 'them' as those driven off.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -tu ending marks the doer as 'I' (first-person singular completed action). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural). So it states a completed act of driving 'them' away by 'me'.
7.root: ط-ر-د (ṭ-r-d) — drive away, expel, repel

8.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
8.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) take heed, bear in mind, call to remembrance' — to reflect and let something sink in as a reminder.
9.grammar: A present-tense Form V verb (tafaʿʿala type, whose stem ta- is dropped by assimilation after the present-tense prefix). The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' as the doers in the ordinary (indicative) present, describing ongoing or habitual action.
9.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: 'I say' — the act of speaking or stating, performed by the speaker about himself.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'a-' prefix meaning 'I'. The '-u' ending is the ordinary present-tense form for an ongoing or habitual action: 'I say / I am saying'.

3.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

4.meaning: 'With me / in my possession / in my keeping' — a word indicating presence, possession, or being at hand with the speaker. It points to what one has, holds, or holds as a view.

parts.en: at / with / in the possession of

4.grammar: An adverb of place/possession ('with, at, in the keeping of') joined to the possessive pronoun '-ī' ('me / my'). The base عِنۡدِ carries a short 'i' vowel (kasra) before the suffix, so the segment is read 'ʿindi'; with the attached '-ī' the whole word means 'with me / in my possession'.
4.root: — (adverb of place/possession; no triliteral verbal root)

5.meaning: 'Treasuries / storehouses' — the plural of a vault or repository where precious things and provisions are stored and kept safe. Figuratively, the hidden reserves or stores of something.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'treasuries / storehouses'. The final '-u' is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or stands as the thing being identified.
5.root: خ-ز-ن (kh-z-n) — storing, hoarding, safekeeping

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

8.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
8.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

9.meaning: 'The unseen / the hidden realm' — that which is absent from perception and beyond the reach of the senses: what is concealed, future, or known only to Allah. A central term for the realm hidden from human sight.
9.grammar: A definite noun marked by 'al-' ('the'). The '-a' ending is the accusative case, the form a noun typically takes when it is the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. known, possessed, or sought).
9.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — being hidden, absent, beyond perception

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: 'I say' — the act of speaking or stating, performed by the speaker about himself.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'a-' prefix meaning 'I'. The '-u' ending is the ordinary present-tense form for an ongoing or habitual action: 'I say / I am saying'.
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speaking, uttering

12.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
12.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

13.meaning: 'An angel' — a created being of light who serves and obeys Allah and carries out His commands. The word denotes a heavenly messenger-servant.
13.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the indefinite nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
