13.root: أ-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k) — to convey a message; hence a messenger-angel (also discussed under م-ل-ك)

14.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
14.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

15.meaning: 'I say' — the act of speaking or stating, performed by the speaker about himself.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'a-' prefix meaning 'I'. The '-u' ending is the ordinary present-tense form for an ongoing or habitual action: 'I say / I am saying'.

16.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
16.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

17.meaning: "You regard as lowly / look down upon / despise" — to view someone with contempt as insignificant or beneath notice.
17.grammar: A Form VIII (iftaʿala) present-tense verb from the root z-r-y; in this pattern the original tāʾ assimilates after the zāy, producing the 'zd' cluster (izdarā). The ta- prefix marks the doer as 'you' (second-person masculine singular), and the weak ending -ī reflects the root's final weak letter. It conveys the ongoing act of holding someone in contempt.

18.meaning: "Your eyes" — the eyes (organs of sight), here possessed by a plural 'you'. By extension the word can connote how things appear in people's sight or estimation.
18.grammar: A noun in its broken (irregular) plural form 'eyes'. The -u before the pronoun is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as a subject or as standing on its own. The attached -kum is the possessive 'your', addressed to a group (masculine plural).

19.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
19.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.
19.root: — (particle)

20.meaning: "He gives them / grants them" — to bestow, hand over, or grant something, with an attached 'them' as the recipients.
20.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb (yuʾtiya, 'to cause to come / bestow'); the prefix yuʾ- marks 'he' as the doer and already carries the stem's hamza. The -a vowel on the stem is the subjunctive, the mood used after particles meaning 'that / so that / in order to', giving a sense of 'that he should give'. The attached -humu is 'them' (its final vowel adjusted for the word that follows).
20.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — come; (causative) bring, give

21.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
21.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

22.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
22.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

23.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole and absolute Deity worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a name, not a common noun, and refers to the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
23.grammar: The proper divine name. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject (the doer) of a sentence or the noun being identified.

24.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
24.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

25.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
25.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

26.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
26.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

27.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
27.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
27.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

28.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
28.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

29.meaning: In that case / then — a response particle signaling that what follows is the consequence of a just-stated condition or supposition ('if so, then…').
29.grammar: A response/consequence particle, not a noun or verb. The -an ending is a fixed part of the word (written with a final alif), not a live grammatical case. It introduces the result side of a hypothetical ('then you would…').

30.meaning: A combination meaning 'surely among / truly from' — an emphatic affirmation ('indeed') joined to the word 'from/among', marking belonging to a group or origin from a source.
30.grammar: Two particles together: an emphatic la- ('surely') and the preposition min ('from/among'). Particles take no case ending. Min is normally written 'min' but appears as 'mina' when the next word begins with 'al-' ('the'), to ease pronunciation.

31.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
31.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: "O Nūḥ" — a direct address (a call) to the Prophet Noah, by name.
2.grammar: The particle yā is the vocative 'O', used to call or address someone directly. The name takes the -u ending typical of a singular noun being addressed by name. Together it is a direct summons of Nūḥ.

3.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

4.meaning: "You disputed/argued with us" — to contend, debate, or wrangle with another, with an attached 'us' as the other party in the argument.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb of the mutual-action pattern (jādala), which implies two sides going back and forth — hence 'dispute with'. The -ta ending marks the doer as 'you' (masculine singular, completed action). The attached -nā is the object 'us'.

5.meaning: "And you did much / multiplied (it)" — to make something abundant or to do it a great deal, prefixed with 'and/so'.
5.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'and so / then', linking to what precedes with a sense of consequence. The verb is a past-tense causative ('to make much / do abundantly'); its -ta ending marks the doer as 'you' (masculine singular, completed action).
5.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — be much, many, abundant

6.meaning: "Disputing with us / argument with us" — the verbal noun for the act of contending or debating, with an attached 'us' as the other party.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action 'arguing/disputing'). The -a ending here is the accusative, which commonly marks a noun as the object of a verb or as a specifying complement. The attached -nā is 'us / our', identifying the party disputed with.

7.meaning: "so bring us / then bring to us" — the connective "so/then" plus the command "bring!", with "us" as the one brought to.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male; the bare stem ending in -i is the imperative form ("bring!"). The suffix -nā is the object "us," and the leading fa- means "so/then," linking it as a consequence.
7.root: ا-ت-ي (ʔ-t-y) — to come; (with object) to bring

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
8.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

9.meaning: "you promise us / you threaten us" — the present-tense act of pledging or warning of something to come, by a single "you," with "us" as recipient.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a single "you" (male) as doer; the -u before the suffix is the indicative present (ongoing/general action). The suffix -nā is the object "us."

10.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
10.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

11.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

12.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

13.meaning: The truthful ones — those who are sincere and speak the truth, whose words and deeds match reality. A plural describing people characterized by truthfulness and sincerity, prefixed with 'the.'
13.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('the ones who are truthful') with the definite article 'the.' The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive (oblique) form: it marks the word either as an object of a verb or as following a preposition or possessive, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
13.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, telling the truth

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: 'He/it brings (something) to you' or 'it comes to you' — the act of coming to, or bringing something to, a group of recipients. The single attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all') is the complement of the verb; the thing brought is not a separate pronoun within the word but is understood from context.
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb: the 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the attached '-kum' is the complement 'you all' (male/mixed group). The word contains only the subject prefix, the verb stem, and this '-kum' suffix — there is no separate 'it/him' object pronoun built in. So it conveys 'he/it comes to you' or 'he/it brings (it) to you'.

4.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
4.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
5.root: — (proper divine name)

6.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
6.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
7.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.
7.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

9.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

10.meaning: Active participle meaning 'ones who render (something) powerless / unable to be caught', i.e. those who frustrate or thwart a pursuer and escape beyond reach. The prefixed 'bi-' is a preposition often used to govern such a predicate.
10.grammar: A plural active participle from a causative verb meaning 'to render incapable, to frustrate'. The '-īna' ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive state ('ones who…'). The attached 'bi-' is a preposition; here it precedes the predicate, a common construction giving the sense 'are not able to thwart/escape'.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: "It benefits you / profits you" — to be of use or advantage to someone, with an attached plural 'you' as the one benefited.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb: the ya- prefix marks a masculine 'he/it' as the doer and the -u ending marks the plain present/future indicative ('benefits / will benefit'). The attached -kum is the object 'you' (masculine plural).

3.meaning: "My sincere counsel / good advice" — earnest, well-meaning advice offered for someone's genuine good, with an attached 'my'.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'sincere counsel'. The attached -ī is the possessive 'my'. The kasra (the short 'i' vowel) on the final root letter is the visible genitive case ending, which is retained before the first-person 'my' suffix.

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: "I wanted / I intended" — to want, will, or purpose something, expressed as a completed act by 'I'.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb of the 'will / intend' pattern (arāda). The -tu ending marks the doer as 'I' (first-person singular, completed action). It states a completed act of wanting or intending.
5.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — seek, want, intend

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: "To give sincere counsel / advise (for one's good)" — to offer honest, well-meaning advice.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb with the first-person 'I' prefix (here in its 'a-' form). The -a ending is the subjunctive, the mood used after words meaning 'that / to', so it reads 'that I should advise / to advise'. It conveys the speaker's act of offering sincere counsel.
7.root: ن-ص-ح (n-ṣ-ḥ) — sincerity, sincere counsel

8.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

9.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
9.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

10.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

10.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
11.root: — (proper divine name)

12.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
12.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
12.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: "He leads you astray / lets you go astray" — to cause someone to err, mislead them or let them fall into error, with an attached plural 'you' as the one misled.
14.grammar: A Form IV present-tense causative verb ('to make someone go astray'); the yu- prefix marks 'he' as the doer. The -a vowel on the stem (yughwiya) is the subjunctive, used after particles like 'that / if / in order to'. The attached -kum is the object 'you' (masculine plural).
14.root: غ-و-ي (gh-w-y) — go astray, err, be misled

15.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
15.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

16.meaning: "Your Lord" — the Lord, i.e. the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, provides for and governs all that is, with an attached plural 'your'. Rabb conveys ownership together with loving upbringing and care.
16.grammar: A noun, 'Lord'. The -u before the pronoun is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as a subject or as standing on its own. The attached -kum is the possessive 'your', addressed to a group (masculine plural).
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master; to nurture, sustain

17.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
17.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

18.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
18.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

3.meaning: A past-tense verb with an object pronoun: 'he forged it / invented it falsely' — he fabricated it as a lie and ascribed it to another. The root is the invention of falsehood and slander.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action in the third-person masculine singular ('he forged'), with the attached pronoun -hu ('it/him') as its direct object. The form (built on an added t-) intensifies the sense to deliberate fabrication.
3.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, invent falsely, forge a lie

4.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
4.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

5.meaning: If — a particle introducing a condition: it sets up 'if X (happens), then Y'.
5.grammar: A conditional particle ('if') that introduces a supposed case and typically puts the following verb into the jussive (conditional) form. Its base shape is 'in', whose final nūn carries a sukūn and is fully pronounced. When the next word begins with a sukūn-bearing cluster, the otherwise-quiescent nūn is given a kasra (-i) to avoid two consecutive sukūns meeting (the 'meeting of two quiescents'); this helping vowel eases pronunciation and carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

6.meaning: "I fabricated it / invented it as a lie" — to forge or concoct a falsehood and attribute it falsely, with an attached 'it' as the thing fabricated.
6.grammar: A Form VIII past-tense verb of the 'concoct / forge' pattern (iftarā), with a built-in sense of inventing falsehood. The -tu ending marks the doer as 'I' (first-person singular, completed action). The attached -hu is the object 'it/him'.

7.meaning: "Then upon me / so on me (lies the responsibility)" — a preposition meaning 'on / upon', often carrying the sense of an obligation or burden resting on someone, with an attached 'me', prefixed by 'then/so'.
7.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so', often introducing a result. ʿalā is the preposition 'on / upon', frequently implying a duty or burden; before the attached 'me' it takes the form ʿalay-, and joining with the first-person pronoun produces the doubled 'ya' ('upon me').

8.meaning: "My crime / my sin / my wrongdoing" — the committing of a grave offense or sin, the verbal noun of 'to sin/transgress', with an attached 'my'.
8.grammar: A verbal noun naming the act of committing crime or sin. The attached -ī is the possessive 'my'. The kasra (the short 'i' vowel) on the final root letter is the visible genitive case ending, which is retained before the first-person 'my' suffix.
8.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — commit a crime, sin, transgress

9.meaning: And I — the standalone first-person singular pronoun 'I,' here joined by 'and.' As a detached pronoun it stands on its own (typically as subject), unlike the attached endings.
9.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' 'anā' is the independent (detached) pronoun 'I,' used for emphasis or to begin/identify the subject; it does not take a case ending and is fixed in form.

10.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'free of / quit of / disassociated from' — innocent of and having nothing to do with something, washing one's hands of it. It describes a person clear and detached from a thing, especially a wrong.
10.grammar: A descriptive noun, indefinite, with the nominative -un ending (tanwīn). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('[someone] is free/quit'); the -un tanwīn shows it is indefinite. It is usually completed by 'of/from' something.
10.root: ب-ر-ء (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, quit of; innocence, disassociation

11.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
11.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

12.meaning: "You commit crimes / you sin" — to perpetrate grave wrongs or sins, addressed to a group 'you'.
12.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb of the 'commit crime' pattern. The tu- prefix plus the -ū…-na ending together mark the doer as 'you all' (masculine plural). The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling the plain present/future ('you commit / will commit').
12.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — commit a crime, sin, transgress

1.meaning: A verb meaning 'and it has been revealed / and it was inspired' — passive, expressing that a divine communication has been sent down or conveyed into someone from Allah, without naming the giver. The wa- is a connector ('and'). The content of inspiration is received, not initiated by the one it reaches.
1.grammar: Past-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it was revealed'). The initial vowelled hamzah plus the internal vowelling (ū…i) marks the passive voice — the grammatical subject is the thing revealed, while the revealer is left unstated. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
1.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, inspire, convey by inspiration

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
2.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

3.meaning: Noah — the proper name of the Prophet Nūḥ.
3.grammar: A proper name. The -in ending (nunation) shows it is treated as a fully declinable noun in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding word. (Most personal names are partly indeclinable, but this short name takes full case endings.)

4.meaning: 'That He …' — an emphatic particle meaning 'that / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'he'; it introduces and affirms a clause reporting something about a single masculine subject (most often Allah).
4.grammar: The emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun '-hu' ('he/it') as its subject. 'Anna' introduces a subordinate clause ('… that He …') and gives it certainty; '-hu' identifies a single masculine subject. (The pronoun is pronounced '-hu' here following the 'a' vowel.)

5.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
5.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: "He believes / comes to faith" — to have faith, to trust and affirm as true, especially faith in Allah, the inward security of belief.
6.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb of the 'have faith' pattern (āmana); the yu- prefix marks 'he' as the doer. The -a ending is the subjunctive, the mood used after particles meaning 'that / until / so that', giving a sense of 'that he should believe'.
6.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — be secure, safe; (faith) believe, trust

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
7.root: — (preposition)

8.meaning: "Your people / your folk" — one's people, kinfolk or community, with an attached singular 'your'.
8.grammar: A noun, 'people / folk'. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition. The attached -ka is the possessive 'your' (masculine singular).

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

11.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
11.root: — (no triliteral root; an emphasizing particle)

12.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.

13.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
13.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

14.meaning: "You feel distressed / grieve / despair" — to be saddened, dejected or filled with misery over something.
14.grammar: A Form VIII (iftaʿala) present-tense verb of the 'feel misery' pattern. The ta- prefix marks 'you (singular)' or a feminine 'it/she' as the doer. Its vowelless ending (-is, jussive) is the form taken after particles like 'do not' or 'so', often giving a command or prohibition sense ('do not grieve').

15.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
15.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

16.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
16.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: They do / they were doing — a verb of general doing or acting, performing a deed.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb in the basic Form I. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a 3rd-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the -ūna ending is the indicative mood (a plain statement). The verb is the general one for doing, making, or carrying out an action.
17.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

1.meaning: "And make / build / construct" — a command to fashion, manufacture or build something with skill and care, prefixed with 'and'.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The verb is a direct command ('make! / build!') addressed to one person (masculine singular). Its base ends in a silent consonant, but here it carries a helping -i vowel to ease pronunciation before the next word.

2.meaning: The ship, ark, or vessel — a boat that travels on water. The noun is unusual in that the same form serves for both singular ('a ship') and plural ('ships').
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks a noun as the direct object of a verb or the subject after certain particles.
2.root: ف-ل-ك (f-l-k) — that which is round or revolves; hence both a sailing ship and the orbiting celestial sphere.

3.meaning: 'With/under Our eyes' — an idiom for being kept under loving, protective oversight and supervision; the literal sense is the organs of sight.
3.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with/by/under'. Because it is a preposition, the following noun takes the genitive -i ending. The plural noun aʿyun ('eyes') is then linked to the attached pronoun -nā ('our'), which serves as a possessor.
3.root: ع-ي-ن ('-y-n) — eye; by extension a spring of water and the essence of a thing.

4.meaning: 'And Our revelation/inspiration' — waḥy is divinely communicated guidance, an unveiling of God's word or prompting placed into a recipient swiftly and secretly.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The noun waḥy carries the genitive -i ending (typically signalling 'of …' or following a preposition), here linking it to the attached pronoun -nā ('our') as possessor.
4.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to convey swiftly and inwardly; inspiration, revelation, a subtle communication.

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: 'You address/speak to Me' — to speak directly to someone, to enter into discourse or plead with them, addressed to a single 'you'.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form III (the type that implies acting toward another party). The tu- prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you'). The stem ends with no vowel (sukūn), the jussive mood, which appears after particles of prohibition or condition (e.g. 'do not …'). The attached -nī is the object 'me'.
6.root: خ-ط-ب (kh-ṭ-b) — to address, to speak formally; also a discourse, sermon, or marriage proposal.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
9.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

10.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
10.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

11.meaning: 'Drowned ones' / 'those who are to be drowned' — people overwhelmed and submerged by water. As a passive participle it names the undergoer of the action, not its doer.
11.grammar: A Form IV passive participle ('one who is drowned'). The mu- prefix forms the participle; the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence.
11.root: غ-ر-ق (gh-r-q) — to sink, drown, be submerged or overwhelmed.

1.meaning: 'And he makes/constructs' — to fashion, build, or manufacture something with skill and craft; ṣanaʿa implies deliberate workmanship.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual present-tense action (a plain statement of fact, with the verb under no governing particle).
1.root: ص-ن-ع (ṣ-n-ʿ) — to make, craft, manufacture; skilled workmanship.

2.meaning: The ship, ark, or vessel — a boat that travels on water. The same form serves for both singular ('a ship') and plural ('ships').
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks a noun as the direct object of a verb or the subject after certain particles.
2.root: ف-ل-ك (f-l-k) — that which is round or revolves; hence both a sailing ship and the orbiting celestial sphere.

3.meaning: 'And whenever / and every time' — a compound expressing that something recurs each and every time a condition is met.
3.grammar: A fixed compound that functions as a conjunction of repetition ('every time that …'). It is built from kulla ('every', carrying an -a ending) joined to the particle mā; together they introduce a clause whose action repeats on every occurrence of the following event.
3.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, the whole, allness (from kull).

4.meaning: he passed / he passed by — a third-person past verb meaning to go past, to pass through or by a place or thing.
4.grammar: A past tense verb with a third-person singular masculine doer ('he'). The doubled final consonant reflects the root's repeated letter. The final -a marks the third-person singular masculine subject. It states a completed action: 'he passed'.
4.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass, to pass by

5.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
5.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

6.meaning: The leading men, chiefs, or notables of a people — the prominent assembly whose standing and counsel fill the eyes and command attention; also a council of elites.
6.grammar: A noun bearing the ending -un (here written -on), which combines the nominative case (typically the subject of a sentence) with nunation — the final -n that marks the noun as indefinite ('a/an …').
6.root: م-ل-أ (m-l-ʾ) — to fill, fullness; hence those who fill an assembly with their eminence.

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
8.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

9.meaning: 'They scoffed / ridiculed / made fun.' The verb sakhira means to mock or deride, to treat someone with scornful laughter.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending (written with a silent trailing alif) marks a completed act by 'they' (masculine plural). It denotes treating someone with mockery and scorn.
9.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to mock, deride, scoff (also: to subject/press into service)

10.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
10.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

11.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
11.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: 'You (all) mock/ridicule' — to scoff at, deride, or treat someone with contempt and derision, addressed to a group.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The dropped final -n (the bare -ū rather than -ūna) shows the subjunctive or jussive mood, used after particles such as 'if' or 'so that'.
13.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to mock, deride; also to subject or press into service.

14.meaning: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
14.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
14.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

15.meaning: Then indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis and a connecting 'then/so'. The particle inna strongly affirms the statement, while the prefix fa- ties it as a consequence to what came before.
15.grammar: The connective fa- ('then, so', often marking a result) prefixed to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly'), with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The whole emphatically asserts a statement about 'we' as a consequence.

16.meaning: 'We mock/ridicule' — to scoff at, deride, or treat with contempt, with 'we' as the doer.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain present-tense statement (the verb under no governing particle).
16.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to mock, deride; also to subject or press into service.

17.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
17.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
17.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

18.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
18.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

19.meaning: 'You (all) mock/ridicule' — to scoff at, deride, or treat someone with contempt, addressed to a group.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix together with the full -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all') in the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action, with the final -n retained because no governing particle shortens it.
19.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to mock, deride; also to subject or press into service.

1.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
1.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

2.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
2.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

4.meaning: 'It comes to him / will come to him' — the act of arriving at or reaching a person, with an attached 'him' as the one reached.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he comes'). The attached -hi is the object 'him' (the -i vowel of this pronoun appears after an -i sound). The form is read as a sound (indicative/subjunctive) present rather than a command.
4.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring; to reach or befall.

5.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.
5.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

6.meaning: 'It disgraces him / will disgrace him' — to bring shame, humiliation, and abasement upon someone; an attached 'him' is the one disgraced.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form IV (the causative type — to 'bring' the state about). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). The attached -hi is the object 'him'. The weak final root letter shows as the long -ī before the pronoun.

7.meaning: 'And it descends / alights' — to come down upon, settle on, or befall; ḥalla also carries the sense of becoming due or lawful, but here the core is 'to land upon'.
7.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain present-tense statement with no governing particle.
7.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to alight, settle, untie; hence what 'comes down,' and also what is loosed and so permitted.

8.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
8.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

9.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

10.meaning: "lasting, enduring, permanent, abiding" — an active participle describing something that stays in place, persists, or is established and ongoing.
10.grammar: An active participle (form IV) functioning as an adjective/noun ("one that stays, abiding"). The "mu-" prefix marks the doer/agent of the action. The final "-un" (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative ending, marking the word as indefinite ("a lasting one") and as a subject or predicate rather than an object.
10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, remain, establish

1.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
1.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

3.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

4.meaning: 'Our command / our decree / our affair / our matter' — a noun spanning an authoritative order, a divine decree, or simply a matter or affair, belonging to 'us'.
4.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -nā ('our'), showing possession. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used when the word is the subject of a sentence or otherwise the one performing/being identified.

5.meaning: 'And it gushed forth / boiled over' — to surge, well up, and overflow; said of water bursting out or a fire/pot boiling violently.
5.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The remainder is a past-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('it gushed'); the final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he/it' did something.
5.root: ف-و-ر (f-w-r) — to boil, gush, surge up; a sudden welling forth.

6.meaning: The oven, furnace, or baking hearth — a fire-pit or stove for baking; classically also understood as the point from which water burst forth.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'); the leading 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 't' (a 'sun letter'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
6.root: — (an ancient loan-word for a baking oven; no native triliteral root).

7.meaning: 'We said' — the act of speaking or uttering, completed in the past, with 'we' as the speakers (a plural, or the royal/majestic 'We').
7.grammar: A past-tense verb 'to say' with the suffix '-nā' marking the doer as 'we' (first-person plural). This is a hollow verb (its middle root letter is a weak 'w'), which contracts before the suffix to leave 'qul-' before the ending.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

8.meaning: 'Carry! / Load!' — a command to bear, lift, or load something onto a carrier; ḥamala means to take up and transport a burden.
8.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single 'you'. The helping initial 'i-' provides a vowel to begin the word, and the bare stem ending with no final vowel (sukūn) is characteristic of the singular command form ('do it!').
8.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, lift a load; also to conceive/bear young.

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'Of every / each' — kull denotes the totality or entirety of a class; with this indefinite ending it means 'every (one)' or 'all'.
11.grammar: A noun bearing the ending -in, which combines the genitive case (used after a preposition or to link 'of …') with nunation — the final -n marking the word as indefinite ('every/any').
11.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, the whole, allness.

12.meaning: 'A pair / two mates' — two of a kind taken together, specifically a male and female couple; zawj is each member of a pair, and this form names two of them.
12.grammar: A dual noun — Arabic has a special form meaning exactly 'two'. The -ayni ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive case (the object form, or the form after a preposition), as opposed to the -āni form used for the subject.
12.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, couple, join; a spouse or one of a matched pair.

13.meaning: Two; the cardinal number 2 (in its masculine dual form), denoting a matched pair.
13.grammar: The number 'two' in dual form. The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive case — the shape used when the word is an object or follows a preposition. The initial 'i' is a helping vowel (a 'connecting hamza') that smooths pronunciation.
13.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — twoness, doubling, a second of a pair

14.meaning: 'And your family / household' — ahl are the people who belong to one: one's family, kin, or the folk closely associated with a place or thing.
14.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The noun ahl carries the accusative -a ending (typically marking a direct object), and the attached -ka is the possessor 'your' (addressed to a single male).
14.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinfolk, the people belonging to a household or place; being fit/worthy.

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

16.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
16.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
16.root: — (pronoun)

17.meaning: It went before, preceded, came earlier in time or rank; to get ahead of or outrun. It also conveys a prior decree or word that has already gone forth and settled a matter in advance.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he/it' as subject. The plain -a ending is the basic past-tense form, reporting a completed action.

18.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
18.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

19.meaning: The word, the saying, the utterance — a statement or pronouncement; qawl is speech that has been spoken, and 'the word' can mean a settled decree or verdict.
19.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
19.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; a saying, statement, or pronouncement.

20.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
20.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
20.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

21.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.

22.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
22.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

23.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.

24.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
24.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

25.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
25.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

26.meaning: 'Few', 'little', 'a small amount/number'. Describes something scant in quantity — a small group of people or a small portion of a thing.
26.grammar: A descriptive adjective (or noun). The '-un' ending is the nominative case with nunation ('tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a few', not 'the few'); the nominative typically marks the subject or a predicate.

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: 'Embark! / Ride! / Board!' — a command to a group to mount or get aboard a conveyance; rakiba means to ride or board a vehicle, beast, or ship.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The helping initial 'i-' supplies a starting vowel, and the -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('all of you, do it!').
2.root: ر-ك-ب (r-k-b) — to ride, mount, board; a rider or mounted party.

3.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
3.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

4.meaning: 'In the name of …' — the standard phrase invoking a name as one begins an act, dedicating the deed to and seeking blessing through the one named.
4.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'in/with/by'. Because it is a preposition, the following noun ism ('name') takes the genitive -i ending, which links it onward to a following possessor ('the name OF …'). The initial hamza of ism is dropped in writing after the prefix.
4.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, elevation; the source of ism ('name') and samāʾ ('sky').

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: Its sailing, its running on a course — a noun naming the place, time, or act of moving along (as a ship over water), with an attached possessive 'its' referring to a feminine thing.
6.grammar: A noun of place/time on the pattern mafʿal, meaning the place, time, or manner of running/sailing. The suffix -hā is an attached possessive pronoun, 'its/her,' referring to a feminine noun. This noun comes from a weak (defective) root and in isolation ends in a shortened alif (majrā); when the pronoun -hā attaches, that final alif shortens to -a, giving the bound stem majra-.
6.root: ج-ر-ي (j-r-y) — to flow, run, sail, course along

7.meaning: And its anchoring, its coming-to-rest — a noun naming the place, time, or act of dropping anchor and halting (as a ship), with an attached possessive 'its,' prefixed with 'and.'
7.grammar: A noun of place/time on the pattern mufʿal, derived from a Form IV verb meaning 'to anchor/make fast,' indicating the place, time, or manner of anchoring. The prefix wa- means 'and.' The suffix -hā is an attached possessive 'its/her' for a feminine referent. From a weak root, the noun ends in a shortened alif in isolation (mursā); before the pronoun -hā that alif shortens to -a, giving the bound stem mursa-.
7.root: ر-س-و (r-s-w) — to be firm, stand fast, anchor

8.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
8.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

9.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
9.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

10.meaning: Surely most forgiving — abundantly and repeatedly forgiving, One who covers over and pardons sins again and again. The intensive form stresses the fullness and constancy of the forgiving.
10.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic 'surely/indeed' (often answering or stressing a statement). The stem is the intensive adjective 'faʿūl' ('much-forgiving'). The final -un is the nominative case with nunation, typically marking a predicate ('… is surely Most-Forgiving'). It conveys constant, abundant forgiveness.
10.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

11.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').
11.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

1.meaning: And she/it — a stand-alone subject pronoun for a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing or person, prefixed with 'and.'
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person feminine singular, 'she' or 'it.' Such pronouns stand alone as the subject or topic of a sentence and do not take case endings. The prefix wa- is the connective 'and.'

2.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

3.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
3.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: A wave, a surge of water — a swelling crest of the sea; the singular noun for billowing, heaving water.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -in (tanwīn with kasra) marks it as both indefinite ('a wave') and in the genitive case — the case that typically follows a preposition or links one noun to another in an 'of' relationship.
5.root: م-و-ج (m-w-j) — to surge, billow, heave (of water)

6.meaning: Like the mountains — a comparison phrase meaning 'resembling the mountains,' evoking great towering masses.
6.grammar: A noun (plural of jabal, 'mountain') made definite by al- ('the') and governed by the prefixed comparison particle ka- ('like, as'). Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the genitive ending -i, required here by that particle.

7.meaning: And he called out, he summoned — past-tense action of raising the voice to call to someone, prefixed with 'and.'
7.grammar: A Form III past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, 'he called out.' Form III often carries the sense of directing an action toward someone. The final -ā is the fixed ending of this verb from a weak root; the prefix wa- means 'and.'
7.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w/y) — to call, summon, cry out

8.meaning: Nūḥ — the proper name of the Prophet Noah.
8.grammar: A proper name functioning as the subject (doer), shown by the nominative ḍamma. As a foreign (non-Arabic) proper name, Nūḥ is classically a diptote — a noun that does not take tanwīn (nunation) — so in careful classical grammar it carries a bare ḍamma (-u) without the -n sound in the nominative.

9.meaning: His son — the noun 'son' carrying an attached 'his.' The leading hamza is a connecting (helping) hamza that smooths pronunciation.
9.grammar: A noun, 'son,' with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The ending -a is the accusative case, typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The initial alif carries a connecting hamza, pronounced only when starting speech.

10.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: A place of seclusion, a spot set apart — a position of standing aside, away and isolated from others.
12.grammar: A noun of place on the pattern mafʿil, meaning 'a place of separation/seclusion.' The ending -in (tanwīn with kasra) marks it indefinite ('a place apart') and genitive — the case used after prepositions or in an 'of' relationship.
12.root: ع-ز-ل (ʿ-z-l) — to set apart, isolate, remove

13.meaning: O my little son — a tender, affectionate address to one's son, combining the vocative 'O' with the diminutive of 'son' and 'my.' The diminutive form conveys endearment rather than smallness.
