When it takes the pronoun -him in a possessive-style (iḍāfa) link, the nunation drops and the participle's inherent final -ī remains; the genitive (linking) case falls on the attached -him ('them'), the ones it comes to.
11.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, arriving

12.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
12.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

13.meaning: 'Other than, except, not' — a word of exception or difference that sets one thing apart from another, or negates an attribute ('non-…').
13.grammar: A noun of exclusion meaning 'other than.' It governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than ___ '). The '-u' nominative ending typically reflects its agreement with, or role describing, a preceding nominative noun.

14.meaning: Turned back, repelled, sent away; something that is averted or refused.
14.grammar: A passive participle ('that which is turned away'). The final -in (nunation) marks an indefinite noun in the genitive (linking) case, typical after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship.

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: she/it came / arrived. A verb of coming, arriving, or presenting itself, in the feminine.
2.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -t marks a single feminine subject: 'she/it came.' Past tense presents the arrival as already accomplished.

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'messengers' joined to 'our' — those sent with a message or commission, envoys; in scripture, the prophets sent by Allah. The form means 'our messengers.'
3.grammar: rusul is the plural of rasūl ('messenger/envoy'). The vowel -u before the pronoun is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject/doer ('the messengers [did]…'). The attached -nā is the possessive 'our.'
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one sent with it

4.meaning: Lut (Lot), the prophet, named as the object/recipient of an action.
4.grammar: A proper name in the object case: the final -an (nunation) marks it as the direct object of a verb (the one to whom or about whom the action is done). As a name it has no root.

5.meaning: He/it was made to feel bad, grieved, or troubled; the experience of being distressed by something.
5.grammar: A passive past-tense verb ('he was distressed/made to feel ill at ease'); the inner vowel shift to -ī- marks the passive of a hollow verb (one with a weak middle root letter). Third-person masculine singular ('he/it') is shown by the absence of any added subject suffix (a zero ending); the final fatḥa is simply the vowel on the last root letter.
5.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — being bad, evil, distressing

6.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
6.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

7.meaning: And it became narrow/tight; the act of being constrained or straitened, joined by 'and'.
7.grammar: Past-tense hollow verb (one with a weak middle root letter). Third-person masculine singular ('he/it') is shown by the absence of any added subject suffix (a zero ending); the final fatḥa is just the vowel on the last root letter. The prefixed wa- is the connective 'and'. Often paired with 'dharʿan' to mean 'felt unable to cope'.
7.root: ض-ي-ق (ḍ-y-q) — narrowness, tightness, constraint

8.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
8.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

9.meaning: In capacity or ability to cope — literally the reach of one's arm; used to specify the respect in which one feels constrained ('straitened in coping').
9.grammar: A noun in the accusative used as a specifier ('as to one's coping-capacity'), clarifying in what respect something applies. The final -an (nunation) marks this indefinite accusative of specification.
9.root: ذ-ر-ع (dh-r-ʿ) — the forearm; by extension, capacity or ability to cope

10.meaning: And he said; the act of speaking or saying, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
10.grammar: Past-tense hollow verb (one with a weak middle root letter). Third-person masculine singular ('he') is shown by the absence of any added subject suffix (a zero ending); the final fatḥa is just the vowel on the last root letter. The prefixed wa- is the connective 'and'.

11.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
11.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

12.meaning: 'a day' — a period of daylight, a single day, or more broadly an appointed time or epoch. It can refer to an ordinary day or to a momentous, decisive day.
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ('a day'): the doubled-n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite, and the -u vowel typically marks it as the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

13.meaning: Hard, severe, distressful; describing a day or event that is extremely trying and difficult to bear.
13.grammar: An adjective of the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern ('exceedingly hard'). The final -un (nunation) marks an indefinite noun in the subject/predicate case ('a distressful one').
13.root: ع-ص-ب (ʿ-ṣ-b) — binding tightly; hence a day that is gripping and severe

1.meaning: And he/it came to him; the act of arriving at someone, joined by 'and', with a masculine subject.
1.grammar: Past-tense verb (with a weak final root letter). Third-person masculine singular ('he/it came') is shown by the absence of any added subject suffix (a zero ending); the final fatḥa is the vowel on the last root letter. The attached -hu means 'him' as the one reached, and the prefixed wa- is the connective 'and'.

2.meaning: 'his people / his folk' — the community, kinsfolk, or nation belonging to him.
2.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/community' with the attached pronoun -hu ('his') marking possession. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the noun as the subject — the one performing the action.

3.meaning: They are driven/hurried along, rushing as if urged on; moving with eager, headlong haste.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb ('they are made to hurry'). The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the -na shows the ordinary (indicative) present.
3.root: ه-ر-ع (h-r-ʿ) — being driven or hurried, rushing

4.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

5.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
5.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

6.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
6.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

7.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
7.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

8.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
8.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
8.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

9.meaning: 'The evil deeds / bad actions' — plural of sayyi'a, a wrong or evil act, a misdeed or sin; the opposite of a good deed.
9.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the misdeeds'). The -i ending here is the case marker for the sound feminine plural in the genitive/accusative state, typically signalling that it follows a preposition, links to a preceding noun, or stands as an object.
9.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; misdeed, wrong

10.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
10.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

11.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
11.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

12.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
12.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

13.meaning: My daughters; the female children of the speaker.
13.grammar: A feminine plural noun with a possessive ending. The attached -ī means 'my', marking the daughters as belonging to the speaker.

14.meaning: 'They / them' — the detached subject pronoun for a group of females, standing on its own to mean 'they (feminine)' or to emphasize the female group as the topic.
14.grammar: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' for a group of females. Because it is a separate word, it normally serves as the subject of a sentence or gives emphasis ('they themselves'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

15.meaning: Purer / more pure; a higher degree of purity and cleanness, whether physical or moral.
15.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the 'afʿal' pattern ('purer / purest'). The final -u marks it in the subject/predicate case.

16.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
16.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

17.meaning: A two-part word: a connecting/result particle 'fa' ('so, then, therefore') joined to a command 'be mindful, guard yourselves, hold in reverent awe.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself from harm or wrongdoing through God-conscious vigilance, keeping a careful, reverent guard.
17.grammar: A result particle 'fa-' attached to an imperative (command) verb, 2nd person masculine plural. The -ū ending directs the command at a group: 'you all, guard yourselves / be mindful.' The 'fa-' frames the command as following from something just stated ('so then...').
17.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
18.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

19.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
19.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

20.meaning: You (plural) shame or disgrace me; bringing humiliation upon someone.
20.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the ordinary (indicative) mood. The tu- prefix with the long -ū marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the final -ni is the object pronoun 'me' (its underlying -ī having been dropped in this spelling), naming the one disgraced.
20.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — disgrace, shame, humiliation

21.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
21.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

22.meaning: My guest(s); the visitor(s) one is hosting — the word can denote one or many.
22.grammar: A noun with a possessive ending. The attached -ī means 'my', marking the guest(s) as those the speaker is hosting.

23.meaning: "Is it not …? / Is … not …?" A questioning "is not," combining the question-marker "a-" with the negative verb "laysa" ("is not"), used to ask a question that expects the answer "yes, it is."
23.grammar: The negating verb laysa ("is/are not") prefixed with the question-marker a- ("…?"). Such "is it not …?" questions typically invite agreement ("yes, indeed it is"). Laysa is a special verb that negates a statement of being; it carries no tense-ending of the ordinary kind here.

24.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
24.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
24.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

25.meaning: A man; an adult male human being.
25.grammar: A singular noun marked indefinite ('a man'). The final -un (tanwīn) combines the -u nominative case-ending — typically marking the doer or subject of a sentence — with the -n that signals indefiniteness ('a man' rather than 'the man').

26.meaning: Rightly guided, sensible, of sound judgment; one who follows the right and mature course.
26.grammar: An adjective of the 'faʿīl' pattern denoting a settled quality ('rightly guided'). The final -un (nunation) marks an indefinite noun in the subject/predicate case ('a right-minded one').
26.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgment, maturity

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
2.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

3.meaning: You (singular) knew / have come to know; the speaker's addressee possesses this knowledge.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ta ending marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you' knew).

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
5.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: Your daughters; the female children belonging to the person addressed.
7.grammar: A feminine plural noun with a possessive ending. The attached -ka means 'your' (addressing one male), marking the daughters as belonging to the one addressed.
7.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — offspring, children (here, daughters)

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: Truth / right / a just claim: that which is real, true, and rightfully due — what genuinely is the case, and what is owed by justice. As an indefinite noun it means 'a right' or 'rightfully', with no article.
9.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -in carries two signals at once: the final -n (called nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a right', not 'the right'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case, the case used after prepositions or to link one noun to another ('… of …').
9.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, what is due/right

10.meaning: "and indeed you / and truly you" — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') joined to the 'you' pronoun, strongly affirming a statement about the person addressed.
10.grammar: An emphatic opening particle (inna) with an attached pronoun. Inna asserts and strengthens the sentence ('it is certainly the case that…') and grammatically takes its noun/pronoun in the accusative; the attached -ka ('you') is that accusative pronoun. The leading wa- is 'and'.

11.meaning: You (singular) surely know; an emphatic affirmation that the addressee possesses this knowledge.
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb with emphatic la- ('surely'). The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'); the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowing, knowledge

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: We want / wish / intend — to desire and purpose something, with an inclination of the will toward it.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb of the Form IV pattern, first-person plural ('we'). Form IV here is not causative in meaning; the verb simply means 'to want / to intend'. The nu- prefix means 'we'. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain ongoing statement. From a hollow root whose middle letter surfaces as the long ī.

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
4.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

5.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
5.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.
5.root: — (preposition; no root)

6.meaning: Strength, power, force, might — physical or military vigour, robustness, and the capacity to exert force or prevail. Also used for firmness and resolve.
6.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the -an ending (the 'tanwīn' or 'n' of indefiniteness), so 'a strength / some power' with no 'the.' The accusative -an form is commonly used to specify in what respect something is meant ('in terms of strength') or as the object of a verb.
6.root: ق-و-ي (q-w-y) — to be strong; strength, power

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: A first-person imperfect verb meaning 'I take shelter, I betake myself to refuge, I withdraw to a place of safety.' It conveys retreating to something that gives protection and security.
8.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb in the first person singular: 'I take refuge / I would take refuge.' The vowel pattern with the long opening 'ā-' marks the speaker as 'I'. The bare ending (no extra suffix) leaves it open to a present or potential sense ('I shelter' / 'I might shelter').
8.root: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, give refuge, retire to a place

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
9.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'a support, a pillar, a firm corner or buttress' — something solid and strong that one can lean on or rely upon for protection.
10.grammar: Singular indefinite noun. The '-in' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a support') and as genitive case, the case typically used after a preposition or when a word is linked as the object 'of' something.
10.root: ر-ك-ن (r-k-n) — to lean on, rely upon; a pillar/mainstay

11.meaning: An adjective meaning 'strong, mighty, intense, severe, firm' — describing something powerful and hard to overcome.
11.grammar: Singular indefinite adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The '-in' ending marks it indefinite and genitive, agreeing with an indefinite genitive noun it describes ('a strong …').
11.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A vocative call meaning 'O Lut!' — addressing the prophet Lūṭ (Lot) by name.
2.grammar: A vocative phrase: the particle 'yā' summons or addresses, and the name takes the '-u' ending characteristic of a single definite person being directly called ('O Lut!').

3.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
3.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

4.meaning: 'Messengers', those sent with a message or mission, especially the prophets sent by Allah. This is the plural of 'rasūl' (an envoy, one dispatched to deliver a message).
4.grammar: A plural noun (plural of 'rasūl'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action ('the messengers …').
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sending, message, messenger

5.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
5.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

6.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
6.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

7.meaning: A third-person plural imperfect verb meaning 'they reach, they arrive at, they attain, they get through to' something.
7.grammar: Imperfect verb, third-person masculine plural. The 'ya-' prefix plus the '-ū' ending together mean 'they (men).' The dropped final nūn (the short '-ū' rather than '-ūna') signals a subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after certain particles meaning 'that they reach' or 'so that they may reach.'
7.root: و-ص-ل (w-ṣ-l) — to reach, arrive, connect, join

8.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
8.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

9.meaning: A command meaning 'travel by night, set out under cover of night.' The verb specifically denotes journeying during the night.
9.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('so/then') joined to a singular masculine command (imperative): 'travel by night!' The final '-i' is the imperative form of this weak-ending verb, directed at one male addressee.

10.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'with your family, with your household / kin.' 'Ahl' denotes one's people, family, and those belonging to a household.
10.grammar: Preposition 'bi-' ('with') + noun + possessive pronoun. The '-i' is the genitive ending required after the preposition 'bi-'; the attached '-ka' means 'your,' addressed to one male.
10.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, household, people belonging to a place

11.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'during a portion / part (of the night),' literally 'in a stretch or segment' — a cut-off piece, here typically a span of time.
11.grammar: Preposition 'bi-' ('in/during') + indefinite noun. The '-in' ending (nunation) marks the noun indefinite ('a portion') and genitive, the case governed by the preposition.
11.root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ) — to cut, sever; a piece/portion

12.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
12.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

13.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
13.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: A third-person/second-person singular imperfect verb meaning 'to turn around, glance back, look behind' — to twist one's head or attention backward.
15.grammar: Imperfect verb of the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he turns/looks back'). The vowelless final 't' (jussive) shows it is governed by a preceding particle, as in a prohibition ('let him not look back') or conditional.
15.root: ل-ف-ت (l-f-t) — to turn, twist; to turn the face/attention

16.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
16.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
16.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

17.meaning: One, a single one, anyone — denotes an individual unit; in negative or questioning contexts it often means 'anyone at all'.
17.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('one'/'anyone') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence.

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: A noun meaning 'your wife / the woman of (a man),' from a word denoting an adult woman. With the possessive it specifies a man's wife.
19.grammar: Feminine noun in a possessive construction with the attached pronoun '-ka' ('your,' to one male). The 'a' that appears before the pronoun is the inherent linking vowel of the feminine ending (tā marbūṭa) that surfaces whenever a suffix is attached; it is present in every case (nominative, accusative, genitive) and so does not by itself mark which case the word is in.
19.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — relating to a person; (feminine) woman

20.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
20.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

21.meaning: An active participle with a pronoun, meaning 'one that will reach / befall her,' i.e. 'a striker/afflicter of her.' It denotes the agent of a calamity that lands upon someone.
21.grammar: Active participle (form IV) — 'the one who/that befalls' — joined to the object pronoun '-hā' ('her'). The '-u' is the nominative ending, the case used for the subject or predicate of a sentence. As a participle it often carries a future/impending sense ('what will strike her').
21.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall, strike (esp. of a calamity)

22.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
22.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

23.meaning: It struck or befell them — said of something (typically an affliction, hardship, or event) that reached and afflicted a group of people. The verb conveys hitting a target or something landing upon someone.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb (he/it did) in the third-person masculine singular, here in its causative 'af'ala' pattern (to make something hit/reach). The attached -hum is an object pronoun meaning 'them', so the whole reads 'it befell them'.
23.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, to be correct/apt; (of rain or affliction) to come down upon

24.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
24.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

25.meaning: A noun meaning 'their appointed time / promised moment / tryst' — a fixed time or place set by promise. With the pronoun it means 'the time appointed for them.'
25.grammar: Noun of time/place (mawʿid) + the pronoun 'their.' The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case used when the word is the object of a verb or the subject of an equational statement being defined. The pronoun has two forms: '-hum' normally, and '-humu' (with a connecting vowel '-u') whenever it is followed by a vowel-initial syllable, to ease pronunciation.
25.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, appoint a time

26.meaning: A noun meaning 'the morning, the daybreak, the early dawn' — the first light of day.
26.grammar: Definite noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject or predicate of a sentence ('the morning [is] …'). Note the article's 'l' assimilates in pronunciation into the following 'ṣ' (a 'sun letter').
26.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning, daybreak; to enter upon morning

27.meaning: "Is it not …? / Is … not …?" A questioning "is not," combining the question-marker "a-" with the negative verb "laysa" ("is not"), used to ask a question that expects the answer "yes, it is."
27.grammar: The negating verb laysa ("is/are not") prefixed with the question-marker a- ("…?"). Such "is it not …?" questions typically invite agreement ("yes, indeed it is"). Laysa is a special verb that negates a statement of being; it carries no tense-ending of the ordinary kind here.

28.meaning: A noun meaning 'the morning, the daybreak, the early dawn' — the first light of day.
28.grammar: Definite noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject or predicate of a sentence ('the morning [is] …'). Note the article's 'l' assimilates in pronunciation into the following 'ṣ' (a 'sun letter').
28.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning, daybreak; to enter upon morning

29.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'near, close at hand' (in time or place) — used to deny or affirm nearness, 'something near.'
29.grammar: Preposition 'bi-' + indefinite adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern. The '-in' ending marks it indefinite and genitive (the case after 'bi-'). This 'bi-' often adds emphasis to a predicate, as in the construction '… is not anything near.'
29.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, close; nearness

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

3.meaning: 'Our command / our decree / our affair / our matter' — a noun spanning an authoritative order, a divine decree, or simply a matter or affair, belonging to 'us'.
3.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -nā ('our'), showing possession. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used when the word is the subject of a sentence or otherwise the one performing/being identified.

4.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
4.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

5.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'its uppermost part, its top side, its highest portion' — the upper surface of a thing, with the pronoun referring back to it.
5.grammar: Active participle of a weak-final root used as a noun ('the high/upper part'), built on the stem 'ʿāliy-' whose final 'y' is the third root consonant (not a long vowel). To this is added the accusative ending '-a' and the pronoun '-hā' ('its'), giving 'ʿāliya-hā.' The accusative is the case used when the word is the object of a verb (e.g., 'We made its top …').
5.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, elevated; height, the upper part

6.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'its lowermost part, its bottom side, its lowest portion' — the under/lower surface of a thing, with the pronoun referring back to it.
6.grammar: Active participle used as a noun ('the low/bottom part') + the pronoun 'its.' The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case used when the word functions as the object of a verb (e.g., 'turned its bottom …').
6.root: س-ف-ل (s-f-l) — to be low, beneath; lowness, the lower part

7.meaning: And We rained down — We caused rain (or something falling like rain) to pour upon a target, often as a sending-down of punishment.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative form ('to make rain fall'), joined by wa- ('and'). The attached -nā marks the doer as 'we'. So it reads 'and We rained down / We sent down (rain) upon'.
7.root: م-ط-ر (m-ṭ-r) — rain, to rain

8.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
8.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

9.meaning: Stones; pieces of rock. This is the broken (irregular) plural of the singular noun ḥajar ('a stone'), denoting stones in the plural.
9.grammar: A feminine broken plural of ḥajar ('stone'), ending in tāʾ marbūṭa. It carries tanwīn fatḥa (the -an ending), the accusative case with 'nunation,' marking an indefinite noun ('stones / some stones') that typically functions as a direct object or specifier of quantity.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'baked clay, hardened stone of clay' — a substance of clay fired hard like stone. Often understood as clay-stone used as a missile.
11.grammar: Singular indefinite noun. The '-in' ending marks it indefinite ('baked clay') and genitive, the case used after a preposition or when linked as 'of' something (e.g., 'stones of baked clay').
11.root: — (commonly held to be of non-Arabic origin; no native triliteral root)

12.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'layered, piled up, set close in successive rows / stacked tightly together.'
12.grammar: Passive participle ('that which has been layered/stacked'). The '-in' ending marks it indefinite and genitive, agreeing with an indefinite genitive noun it describes ('… of stacked [clay]').
12.root: ن-ض-د (n-ḍ-d) — to arrange in layers, pile up, stack in rows

1.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'marked, branded, distinguished by a sign / set apart with a token' — bearing a mark that singles it out.
1.grammar: Passive participle (form II) in the feminine ('marked'). The feminine '-a(t)' agrees with a feminine noun; the '-an' ending (nunation) marks it indefinite and accusative — the case used for objects of verbs and for descriptive states.
1.root: س-و-م (s-w-m) — to mark, brand, set a distinguishing sign

2.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
2.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

3.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

4.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

5.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
5.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
7.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; wrongdoing, injustice

8.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'far, far off, distant' (in place or time) — used especially to deny remoteness, 'something far away.'
8.grammar: Preposition 'bi-' + indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The '-in' ending marks it indefinite and genitive (the case after 'bi-'). The 'bi-' here often emphasizes a predicate, as in '… is not far off.'
8.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be far, distant; remoteness

1.meaning: "and to / toward" — the connective "and" joined to the preposition meaning "to, toward, up to (an end-point)."
1.grammar: A particle cluster: the connective wa- ("and") plus the preposition ilā ("to/toward"), which indicates direction or destination and puts the following noun into the genitive case. Particles do not inflect.

2.meaning: Madyan (Midian) — the proper name of an ancient people and the land they inhabited.
2.grammar: A proper name. As a diptote (not fully declinable) noun, it takes a single -a ending in place of both accusative and genitive and does not receive tanwīn. It names a people and their territory.

3.meaning: "their brother" — the noun "brother" (a male sibling, or by extension a kinsman/fellow member of a community) with the possessor "their."
3.grammar: "Brother" is one of the special "five nouns" whose case is shown by a long vowel: the -ā here marks the accusative (object) state. The suffix -hum means "their," referring to a group of males.

4.meaning: Shuʿayb — the proper name of a prophet sent to the people of Madyan.
4.grammar: A proper name (the diminutive form of a name) that is fully declinable (triptote). The -an ending marks the accusative case — fitting when the name is the one being sent or mentioned as object. The tanwīn here signals that the name belongs to the fully declinable class, not indefiniteness, since a proper name is inherently definite.

5.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
5.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

6.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
6.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

7.meaning: 'Serve!,' 'worship!,' 'devote yourselves in obedience!' — a command to render worship and humble service. The underlying sense is to submit oneself wholly, in reverence and obedience, to the one served.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending means the order is given to several people: 'you all do it!' The initial vowel is a helping prosthetic vowel that lets the word begin, since the bare command stem would otherwise start with a vowelless letter.
7.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, devotion

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: 'A god / a deity' — any object of worship; the general word for a deity (as opposed to the proper name Allah).
12.grammar: A singular indefinite noun 'a god'. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a/any') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship. It denotes a deity in general.
12.root: ا-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

13.meaning: Other than him, someone or something besides him — denoting difference or exception from a masculine referent.
13.grammar: A noun of exception meaning 'other than', carrying the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. The attached -hu is a genitive pronoun ('him/it') in a possessive-style link, so the whole word reads 'other than him'.

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: A second-person plural imperfect verb meaning 'you (all) diminish, reduce, give short, cut down' — to make something less than its due.
15.grammar: Imperfect verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all diminish'). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ū' ending means 'you (men).' The shortened ending (without final nūn) signals subjunctive/jussive mood, used after particles such as a prohibition ('do not diminish').
15.root: ن-ق-ص (n-q-ṣ) — to decrease, diminish, give less than due

16.meaning: A noun meaning 'the measure, the measuring-vessel, the standard of dry measure' — the instrument or amount by which goods are measured out.
16.grammar: Definite noun with article 'al-' ('the'), on the instrument-noun pattern mifʿāl (a prefixed 'mi-' plus the three root letters with a long 'ā' before the last), which names a tool or means for an action. The '-a' ending is accusative, marking it as the direct object of a verb (e.g., 'do not shortchange the measure').
16.root: ك-ي-ل (k-y-l) — to measure (esp. grain); a measure

17.meaning: 'And the balance / the scales' — the instrument for weighing, and by extension the principle of just weight and equilibrium.
17.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a definite masculine singular noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb. The mīzān pattern (mifʿāl) denotes an instrument — here a thing used for weighing.

18.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
18.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

19.meaning: A past-tense verb from the root of seeing, in the causative sense 'he showed / let you see / made you behold' something. So: 'he caused you (plural) to see'.
19.grammar: A perfect (past) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative (Form IV) pattern ('to make someone see' = to show). The final long vowel of the stem is a weak (defective) root letter. The attached -kum is the object 'you all'.
19.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see; (causative) to show, cause to behold

20.meaning: Good, better, that which is beneficial — goodness itself, and by comparison 'more good / better'; also wealth or any benefit regarded as good.
20.grammar: A noun/comparative ('good' or 'better') carrying a prefixed preposition. The prefix bi- means 'with'; the final -in is the indefinite genitive (nunation), showing no 'the' and the genitive case taken after a preposition.
20.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or preferable

21.meaning: A combination meaning 'and indeed I …' — a connective 'and' joined to an emphatic particle plus 'I,' strongly affirming what the speaker is about to say.
21.grammar: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + the emphatic particle 'inna' ('indeed/truly') + the attached pronoun '-ī' ('I/me'). 'Inna' adds strong affirmation to the statement; the '-ī' is its subject, so the whole reads 'and truly I …'.

22.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

23.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
23.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

24.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
24.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

25.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
25.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
25.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

26.meaning: An active participle meaning 'encompassing, all-surrounding, comprehending everything' — one who encircles a thing completely, in knowledge or in power, leaving nothing outside His grasp.
26.grammar: Active participle (form IV) meaning 'one who encompasses.' The '-in' ending marks it indefinite and genitive — the case used after a preposition or when linked as 'of' something (e.g., 'encompassing of a thing').
26.root: ح-و-ط (ḥ-w-ṭ) — to surround, encircle, encompass, comprehend fully

1.meaning: 'And O my people!' — an affectionate call addressed to one's own community or kinsfolk.
1.grammar: A direct address: 'wa' ('and') plus the vocative particle 'yā' ('O') calling 'qawm' ('people'). The final -i stands in for the possessive 'my' (the 'ī' is shortened/dropped), so it means 'O my people'. 'qawm' is a collective term for one's community.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group / community

2.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'fulfil!', 'discharge in full!', 'pay back completely!'. The verb conveys giving something its complete, undiminished due — meeting an obligation fully without falling short.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb directed at a group of people. The -ū ending marks the command as plural masculine: 'all of you, do this!'. The form is causative/intensive (Form IV), giving the sense of bringing a thing to full completion.
2.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfil completely, to give in full measure, faithfulness

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'the measure, the measuring-vessel, the standard of dry measure' — the instrument or amount by which goods are measured out.
3.grammar: Definite noun with article 'al-' ('the'), on the instrument-noun pattern mifʿāl (a prefixed 'mi-' plus the three root letters with a long 'ā' before the last), which names a tool or means for an action. The '-a' ending is accusative, marking it as the direct object of a verb (e.g., 'do not shortchange the measure').
3.root: ك-ي-ل (k-y-l) — to measure (esp. grain); a measure

4.meaning: 'And the balance / the scales' — the instrument for weighing, and by extension the principle of just weight and equilibrium.
4.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a definite masculine singular noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb. The mīzān pattern (mifʿāl) denotes an instrument — here a thing used for weighing.

5.meaning: In/with justice and equity — 'qisṭ' is fair, balanced dealing: giving each their due in full measure, without wronging anyone.
5.grammar: A masculine noun ('justice, equity') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('in/with') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
5.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — justice, equity, fair measure

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: To diminish or shortchange — to give people less than their due, to defraud or deprive them of part of what is theirs.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you' (the ta- … -ū frame). With its short final -ū (no nūn), it stands in the form used after a negative or prohibitive word, so it carries the sense 'do not shortchange / that you not diminish'.
7.root: ب-خ-س (b-kh-s) — to diminish, give short measure, defraud

8.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
8.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
8.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

9.meaning: Their things — the items, goods, or belongings that pertain to them; the plural of 'thing'.
9.grammar: A plural noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their'). The -a ending marks the accusative case (used for the direct object of a verb); this plural pattern is a diptote and does not take tanwīn. So it reads 'their things / their goods'.
9.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will; the basic notion of 'a thing'

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: A verb meaning to act with corruption, wreak havoc, or work mischief and ruin — to spread disorder and harm.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb directed at a plural 'you' (a group of males or a mixed group). The 'ta-' prefix signals 'you', and the -aw ending marks the plural 'you' subject. The vowelless (cut-off) form here is the mood used after certain particles, e.g. in prohibitions ('do not …').
11.root: ع-ث-و / ع-ث-ي (ʿ-th-w/y) — wreaking corruption and havoc

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
13.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

14.meaning: An active participle (the doer of an action) meaning 'corrupters', 'those who spread corruption' — people who cause ruin, disorder, and moral or social decay.
14.grammar: An active participle on the 'mu-' pattern, naming the one who performs the action of the related verb (to cause corruption). The -īna ending makes it a plural of males in the accusative or genitive case — the form used when the word is an object or otherwise governed, including as a circumstantial description ('… being corrupters').

1.meaning: A remnant or that which is left over after most of something has gone; in religious usage it carries the sense of a lasting, wholesome residue — what truly endures and is best kept.
1.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The tā' marbūṭa carries the ending -u, marking the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate describing it.
1.root: ب-ق-ي (b-q-y) — to remain, endure, be left over

2.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
2.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

3.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
3.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
3.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

4.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
4.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

5.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
5.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

6.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
6.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

7.meaning: Those who have faith — people who believe and trust, specifically those who hold true belief in Allah. An active participle used as a plural noun for 'believers, the faithful.'
7.grammar: A masculine sound plural active participle. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case (sound masculine plurals share one form for both): it signals the word is functioning as an object of a verb, or follows a preposition or a leading noun in a possessive chain.
7.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, faith, to believe / trust

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

9.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
9.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

10.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
10.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

11.meaning: A keeper, guardian, or watchful overseer — one who preserves, protects, and keeps careful watch, maintaining a vigilant record over something.
11.grammar: bi- is a preposition ('with/over') which here often reinforces a negated predicate ('not a guardian over…'), and it puts the following noun in the genitive. ḥafīẓ is an intensive noun of the faʿīl pattern. The -in ending is genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking an indefinite noun governed by the preposition.
11.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — to guard, preserve, protect, keep watch

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A vocative call addressed to a man named Shuʿayb: 'O Shuʿayb!' The opening particle is the standard Arabic 'O…' used to call or address someone.
2.grammar: A direct address: the particle yā ('O') calls the named person. The name carries a final -u, the vowel typically taken by a singular proper name being called in the vocative.

3.meaning: An interrogative opening: 'Is your prayer …?' It combines a yes/no question marker with the noun for the formal worship-prayer (ṣalāh) and an attached 'your'.
3.grammar: A noun with a fronted question particle (a-) and a possessive pronoun suffix. The -u before the suffix is the nominative case, used for the subject; the attached -ka means 'your' addressed to a single male.

4.meaning: 'It commands you' or 'orders you' — a verb expressing that something issues an order, instruction, or bidding to the person addressed, with 'you' as the one commanded.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with a feminine 'it/she' subject (the ta- prefix) and an attached object pronoun 'you' (-ka). The base verb ending is -u (indicative mood), the normal mood for a simple statement of ongoing or habitual action.

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
5.root: — (particle; no root)

6.meaning: 'That we leave / abandon / forsake' — a verb meaning to let go of something, give it up, or cease doing it, with 'we' as the doers.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb with a 'we' subject (the na- prefix). The final -a is the subjunctive mood, the form taken after certain particles such as 'that' or 'in order to,' giving the sense 'that we leave / for us to leave.'
6.root: ت-ر-ك (t-r-k) — to leave, abandon, let go of

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: "he worships / he serves devotedly" — the present-tense act of worship by a single "he" subject.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a single masculine "he" subject; the final -u is the indicative present, expressing an ongoing, habitual, or general action.

9.meaning: Our fathers and forefathers; our ancestors. The word points to the line of male forebears whose example or tradition is often invoked.
9.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our') attached. The plural ends in a hamza (written here on a 'wāw' seat as 'ؤ'), and the '-u' vowel on it before the pronoun is nominative, the case typically used when the noun is the subject (the doer) of a sentence.

10.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
10.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
11.root: — (particle; no root)

12.meaning: 'That we do / make / act' — a verb of doing or carrying out an action, with 'we' as the doers.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb with a 'we' subject (the na- prefix). The final -a marks the subjunctive mood, used after particles like 'that' or 'so that,' giving the sense 'that we do / for us to do.'

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'Our wealth / possessions / properties' — the plural noun for goods, money, and possessions, joined to the pronoun 'our.'
14.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the possessive suffix 'our' (-nā). The -i linking vowel before the suffix is the genitive case, the case taken by a noun that follows a preposition or stands as the possessed term in a chain.

15.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
15.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

16.meaning: 'We wish / will / want' — a verb expressing volition, desire, or choosing, with 'we' as the subject.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb with a 'we' subject (the na- prefix). It expresses willing or wishing, typically as an ongoing or general statement of what 'we want.'
16.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish, want

17.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
17.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

18.meaning: 'Surely you / indeed you' — the second-person pronoun 'you' (one male) reinforced by an emphatic prefix that strengthens and confirms the statement.
18.grammar: A standalone subject pronoun ('you,' one male) carrying the emphatic prefix la- ('surely, indeed'), which underscores and affirms the assertion being made about the addressee.

19.meaning: The Forbearing / the Clement — one who is gentle, patient, and slow to anger, restraining punishment despite the power to act; a being of clemency and self-possessed calm. An intensive adjective denoting deep, habitual forbearance.
19.grammar: A definite adjective/noun of the intensive faʿīl pattern (a quality held deeply and lastingly), with the article al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case, used for the subject or for the predicate that describes the subject ('… is the Forbearing').
19.root: ح-ل-م (ḥ-l-m) — forbearance, clemency, gentle restraint

20.meaning: The Right-minded / Rightly-guiding — one of sound judgment who is on the right course and leads others rightly; mature, sensible, and well-directed. An intensive adjective denoting deep, settled good sense and rectitude.
