20.grammar: A definite noun/adjective of the intensive faʿīl pattern, with the article 'the' (its l assimilates into the following r, hence al-rashīd). The final -u marks the nominative case, used for a subject or a describing predicate ('… is the Right-minded').
20.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgment, maturity

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
2.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

3.meaning: A rhetorical address meaning roughly 'Have you considered?' or 'Tell me — what do you think of…?'. It combines the question particle 'a-' ('do/have…?') with the verb 'to see', here in the sense of mentally considering or reflecting on something rather than literal eyesight. It is addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying a subject built into its ending: the '-tum' ending marks a completed action done by 'you all' (masculine plural). Prefixed with the question particle 'a-', it turns the statement into a question, idiomatically 'have you considered / tell me'.

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'I was / I had been,' the core verb of being placed in the past for the speaker. It links 'I' to a past state or description: 'I used to be / I came to be in such a condition.'
5.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular. The suffix '-tu' is the past-tense ending that means 'I' (the one who did/was). It expresses a completed or settled past state — 'I was, I had been.'
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

7.meaning: A clear proof, plain sign, or self-evident demonstration; something that makes the truth manifest and removes doubt.
7.grammar: A noun (also usable as an intensive adjective) meaning a clear, evident proof. The -in ending is indefinite and genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… of …"), follows a preposition, or follows a quantity word.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, to make plain, distinguish

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: 'My Lord' — the word 'rabb' denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, governs and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached 'my' it expresses one's own Lord and Caretaker.
9.grammar: A noun followed by the possessive ending '-ī' meaning 'my', which joins to the noun and also serves the genitive (possessive) relationship. The attached '-ī' both makes the noun definite and shows ownership: 'my Lord'.

10.meaning: 'And He has provided me / granted me sustenance' — a past-tense verb of providing, bestowing livelihood or provision, with Allah understood as the Provider and 'me' as the recipient.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb (he-form) prefixed by 'and' (wa) and carrying the object pronoun 'me' (-nī). The verb's -a ending is the standard third-person masculine singular past ('he did …'); the linking -n- before 'me' is a connector used with first-person verb objects.
10.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, bestow sustenance / provision

11.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
11.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
11.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

12.meaning: 'provision,' 'sustenance,' 'a means of livelihood' — that which is bestowed to sustain and benefit, such as food and resources. 'Rizq' is whatever Allah grants a creature to live on, material or otherwise.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness — frequently the role of a stated purpose or explanatory complement ('as provision'), telling for what reason or in what capacity something is given.

13.meaning: Good, fine, beautiful, excellent — pleasing and praiseworthy in quality. It describes something done well or possessing goodness and beauty.
13.grammar: An adjective ('good'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite). As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun; the accusative case matches a noun in that same case.

14.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
14.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

15.meaning: I want, I will, I intend, I desire — expressing the speaker's own wish, purpose, or intent.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb. The u- prefix marks the doer as 'I' (the u-vowel is the first-person prefix vowel of this verb's derived pattern). The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing wish or intention ('I want / I am intending').
15.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, will, go after

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
16.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
16.root: — (particle; no root)

17.meaning: 'That I oppose you / go against you / act contrary to you' — a verb meaning to differ from, contradict, or do the opposite of others, with 'I' as the doer and 'you' (plural) as those differed from.
17.grammar: A present-tense Form III verb (the pattern of mutual or directed action, 'to differ-with') with an 'I' subject (the u- prefix) and the object pronoun 'you all' (-kum). The final -a is the subjunctive mood, used after particles like 'that' or 'so as to' — 'that I oppose you.'
17.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to differ, succeed/come after, be at variance

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
18.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

19.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
19.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

20.meaning: 'I forbid you / prohibit you / hold you back' — a verb meaning to forbid, restrain, or warn someone away from something, with 'I' as the one forbidding and 'you' (plural) as those addressed.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb with an 'I' subject (the a- prefix) and the object pronoun 'you all' (-kum). It is a defective verb (its root ends in a weak letter), so the stem closes on a long ā; it expresses a present/ongoing act of forbidding.
20.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, prohibit, restrain

21.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
21.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

22.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
22.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

23.meaning: I want, I will, I intend, I desire — expressing the speaker's own wish, purpose, or intent.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb. The u- prefix marks the doer as 'I' (the u-vowel is the first-person prefix vowel of this verb's derived pattern). The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing wish or intention ('I want / I am intending').
23.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, will, go after

24.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
24.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

25.meaning: Setting right, reform, putting into good order; making peace and amending what is corrupt or broken. A verbal noun denoting the act of improving and rectifying.
25.grammar: A definite verbal noun of Form IV (the 'causing/making' pattern: to make-good, to set-right), with the article 'the.' The final -a marks the accusative case, used when the word is the object of a verb or otherwise governed as a direct complement.

26.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
26.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

27.meaning: 'I was able / had the power / managed to' — a past-tense verb expressing capability or having the strength and means to do something, with 'I' as the subject.
27.grammar: A past-tense Form X verb (the 'seeking/finding-capacity' pattern, here meaning 'to be able') with the suffix -tu marking 'I' as the doer. The -tu ending is the first-person singular past marker: 'I did / I was …'
27.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, be capable

28.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
28.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

29.meaning: 'My granting of success / my being enabled' — the noun for divinely-given success and the bringing of one's efforts into harmony with what is right, joined to 'my.' It conveys success that comes as a granted favour.
29.grammar: A Form II verbal noun (the 'bringing into accord' pattern) with the possessive suffix 'my' (-ī). The -ī ending here is the first-person possessive ('my …'); attaching this pronoun places the noun in the genitive (possessed) state.
29.root: و-ف-ق (w-f-q) — to be in accord, agree, be granted success

30.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
30.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

31.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
31.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
31.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

32.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
32.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

33.meaning: I placed my trust, I relied wholly — to commit one's affairs entirely to another and depend on Him, resting in reliance. The verb's intensive pattern conveys deliberate, complete entrusting.
33.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive intensive pattern (carrying the sense of taking something fully upon oneself — 'to entrust oneself, rely'). The -tu ending means the doer is 'I' and the action is completed.
33.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, appoint as guardian, rely upon

34.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
34.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

35.meaning: 'I turn (repentantly) / I return / I turn back in devotion' — a verb of turning to Allah in repentance and reliance, again and again returning to Him, with 'I' as the subject.
35.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (the 'making oneself turn' pattern) with an 'I' subject (the u- prefix). The final -u is the indicative mood, the normal form for a plain present-tense statement: 'I turn / I am turning.'
35.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — to turn, return, come back repeatedly

1.meaning: 'And O my people!' — an affectionate call addressed to one's own community or kinsfolk.
1.grammar: A direct address: 'wa' ('and') plus the vocative particle 'yā' ('O') calling 'qawm' ('people'). The final -i stands in for the possessive 'my' (the 'ī' is shortened/dropped), so it means 'O my people'. 'qawm' is a collective term for one's community.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group / community

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: A verb with emphatic and attached-object force: 'let it surely not drive/provoke you', 'let it by no means incite you (to wrongdoing)'. The base verb means to carry someone into sin or lead them to commit a crime.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form I (base pattern yaJRImu, 'to drive/incite to sin') carrying two attachments. The doubled-nun 'nna' is the heavy emphatic ending that strengthens the verb to 'shall surely / by no means'; the final 'kum' is an attached object pronoun meaning 'you all' (the ones acted upon).
3.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime/sin; to drive someone into wrongdoing

4.meaning: 'My opposition / my breaking-away / my being at odds' — the noun for discord, schism, and standing on the opposing side, joined to 'my.' It denotes a split into hostile camps.
4.grammar: A Form III verbal noun (the pattern of mutual conflict, 'to be-at-odds-with') with the possessive suffix 'my' (-ī). The -ī ending is the first-person possessive ('my …'), which places the noun in the genitive (possessed) state.
4.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave; discord, opposition

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
5.root: — (particle; no root)

6.meaning: 'That it strike you / befall you / hit you' — a verb meaning for something (often a calamity or affliction) to reach and afflict someone, with 'you' (plural) as those it reaches.
6.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb with an 'it/he' subject (the yu- prefix) and the object pronoun 'you all' (-kum). The final -a is the subjunctive mood, taken after certain particles, giving the sense 'that it befall you / lest it befall you.'
6.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall, afflict

7.meaning: A like, equivalent, or counterpart — something that matches or corresponds to another in measure or kind; 'the equal of'.
7.grammar: A noun meaning 'a like / an equivalent'. The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word stands as a subject or predicate. It commonly heads a possessive phrase ('the like OF …') by linking to a following noun.
7.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similitude, resemblance

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: 'It struck / befell / afflicted' — a past-tense verb describing something (often a punishment or hardship) reaching and hitting its target.
9.grammar: A past-tense Form IV verb in the third-person masculine singular ('it/he …'). The final -a is the standard third-person masculine singular past ending, stating that the action 'struck/befell' has occurred.
9.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall, afflict

10.meaning: a people / folk / nation — a community of people bound together, a group standing as one body; also kinsfolk.
10.grammar: A noun ending in -a, the accusative case — used when the noun is a direct object or otherwise governed in that case. The word is grammatically singular but collective in sense, naming a whole group of people, 'a folk, a nation'.
10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a community that stands together

11.meaning: Noah — the proper name of the Prophet Nūḥ.
11.grammar: A proper name. The -in ending (nunation) shows it is treated as a fully declinable noun in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding word. (Most personal names are partly indeclinable, but this short name takes full case endings.)

12.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
12.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

13.meaning: a people / folk / nation — a community of people bound together, a group standing as one body; also kinsfolk.
13.grammar: A noun ending in -a, the accusative case — used when the noun is a direct object or otherwise governed in that case. The word is grammatically singular but collective in sense, naming a whole group of people, 'a folk, a nation'.
13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a community that stands together

14.meaning: Hūd — a masculine proper name (borne by a prophet sent to the people of ʿĀd). As a name it has no derivable meaning of its own.
14.grammar: A proper name (here the indefinite/nunated form). The -in ending is the genitive case marked with nunation (the -n sound): the genitive is used after prepositions or as the possessed term in a chain ('… of Hud').

15.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
15.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

16.meaning: a people / folk / nation — a community of people bound together, a group standing as one body; also kinsfolk.
16.grammar: A noun ending in -a, the accusative case — used when the noun is a direct object or otherwise governed in that case. The word is grammatically singular but collective in sense, naming a whole group of people, 'a folk, a nation'.
16.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a community that stands together

17.meaning: Ṣāliḥ — a masculine proper name (borne by a prophet sent to the people of Thamūd). The name also literally evokes 'righteous, sound, virtuous,' from a root of wholesomeness.
17.grammar: A proper name (an active participle 'righteous/sound' used as a name), here in the nunated form. The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation (the -n sound), used after prepositions or as the possessed term in a chain ('… of Salih').

18.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
18.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

19.meaning: a people, folk, community; a group of human beings bound together (by kinship, locality, or allegiance). The word often carries the sense of one's own people or nation.
19.grammar: A collective singular noun (singular in form, plural in sense). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject — the one doing or being something in a sentence.
19.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; hence a group that stands together

20.meaning: Lot — the proper name of the Prophet Lūṭ.
20.grammar: A proper name carrying the -in (tanwīn) ending, which marks the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link the name to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
20.root: — (proper name)

21.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
21.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.

22.meaning: 'Far off / distant / remote' — describing something distant in place or time. Often used in the sense 'not far away,' i.e. close at hand, when paired with a negation.
22.grammar: An adjective of the faʿīl pattern preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/in'). The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation (the -n sound), which is required after the preposition bi-; the bi- here commonly adds emphasis to a negative statement ('not at all far').

1.meaning: A call to 'seek forgiveness' — to ask Allah to forgive and cover over one's sins. The Form X pattern conveys actively requesting pardon, joined to a preceding clause by 'and'.
1.grammar: A plural command (imperative) verb, Form X (the ista- pattern, which means 'to seek/ask for' the base action — here 'to seek forgiveness'). The plural wāw (-ū) means 'you (plural masculine), do it!'. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. So: 'and seek forgiveness, all of you'.
1.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

2.meaning: Your Lord — the Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, owns, and cares for you, guiding His servants to completion. "Rabb" carries the joined senses of owner, sustainer, and the one who lovingly brings to maturity, here addressed to a group.
2.grammar: A masculine singular noun with an attached possessive "your" (plural addressee). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case, which generally marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, bring to completion

3.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
3.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

4.meaning: Turn back in repentance — to return to Allah, abandoning wrongdoing and reorienting oneself toward Him (tawba); a command to repent.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, built on a hollow root (its middle letter is a weak wāw). The -ū ending directs the order to a plural 'you all' — 'repent, all of you'.
4.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, return, repent

5.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

6.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
6.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

7.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
7.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

8.meaning: A divine attribute meaning 'most merciful, ever-compassionate' — one who is overflowing with tender mercy and acts mercifully again and again. The pattern faʿīl conveys an intensive, abiding quality, not a passing feeling.
8.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, functioning as a noun/predicate. The final -un (nominative with tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and as the doer or the thing being described — the form a word takes when it is the subject or the predicate of a sentence.

9.meaning: A divine attribute meaning 'most loving, full of love' — one who loves deeply and constantly shows affection. The faʿūl pattern intensifies it, and the sense can be both active (loving others) and reciprocal (worthy of being loved).
9.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿūl pattern, used as a noun/predicate. The final -un (nominative with tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and as a subject or predicate — the form used when the word names the doer or what something is.

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A vocative call addressed to a man named Shuʿayb: 'O Shuʿayb!' The opening particle is the standard Arabic 'O…' used to call or address someone.
2.grammar: A direct address: the particle yā ('O') calls the named person. The name carries a final -u, the vowel typically taken by a singular proper name being called in the vocative.

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: 'We understand / we grasp' — to comprehend deeply, to gain insight into the inner meaning of something rather than merely hear it.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix means the doer is 'we', and the final -u is the indicative ending that marks an ongoing or general action (something we do or are doing). Built on a stem that conveys deep comprehension.
4.root: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h) — to understand deeply, to attain insight

5.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
5.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
5.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

6.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
6.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

7.meaning: You say / you were saying — a present-tense verb of speaking addressed to a single person. It expresses ongoing or habitual utterance.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' (masculine singular) subject, and the final '-u' is the indicative form, used for a plain ongoing statement ('you say'). The long 'ū' is the hollow root's middle letter surfacing.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

8.meaning: And indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis. The particle inna strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, like saying 'truly' or 'most certainly'.
8.grammar: An emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly') with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. The whole strongly asserts a statement about 'we'.

9.meaning: We surely see you / we do see you — an emphatic statement that 'we' perceive a single 'you' (masculine), with an opening particle of emphasis.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb for 'we' (the na- prefix means 'we'), opened by the emphatic la- ('surely/indeed') that strengthens the claim. The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' for a single male. The verb is from a root whose final letter is a weak radical; that radical contracts with the stem into the long vowel ā (written here as rā), so this is not a separable vowel but the assimilated final radical of the root, giving 'we see'.

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'among us / in us / in our midst,' combining the preposition 'in/among' with the pronoun 'us.'
10.grammar: The preposition fī ('in, among, within') with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('us'). Pronouns attached to prepositions are in the object form; the preposition itself does not change shape.

11.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'weak', 'frail', or 'feeble' — lacking strength, whether in body, capacity, or means.
11.grammar: A descriptive noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl, singular indefinite. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn) marks it as 'a weak one' standing as an object, or as a predicate describing someone.
11.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — weakness, feebleness, lack of strength

12.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

12.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

13.meaning: 'Your clan / kinfolk' — a small group of close relatives or supporters (a band of fewer than about ten men), here joined to 'your', i.e. a person's family or following.
13.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is nominative, the form a noun takes when it is the subject or the thing being described. The suffix -ka means 'your' addressed to a single male.
13.root: ر-ه-ط (r-h-ṭ) — a small band of kinsmen

14.meaning: 'We would surely have stoned you' — to pelt or kill someone by throwing stones, stated emphatically as something that would certainly have happened.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb with an emphatic prefix and two pronoun pieces. The la- prefix adds strong emphasis ('surely'). The -nā suffix marks 'we' as the doer of the completed action, and the final -ka is the object 'you' (a single male). The fixed -a inside (rajam-nā) is the normal past-tense stem vowel.
14.root: ر-ج-م (r-j-m) — to stone, to pelt with stones

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

16.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
16.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

17.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
17.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

18.meaning: 'Mighty / strong / dear' — one who is powerful and unassailable, hard to overcome and highly esteemed. The faʿīl pattern gives an intensive, enduring sense.
18.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to an intensive adjective. The final -in is the indefinite genitive ending, which a noun takes after a preposition; the genitive is the case that typically follows prepositions or links a word to a preceding one.
18.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, being unassailable and honoured

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
2.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

3.meaning: 'Is my clan/kinfolk?' — a small group of close relatives joined to 'my', and fronted by a particle that turns the statement into a question.
3.grammar: An interrogative prefix a- ('is…?') on a noun bearing the possessive -ī ('my'). When the possessive 'my' is attached, it replaces the usual case vowel, so the noun ends in -ī regardless of its grammatical role.
3.root: ر-ه-ط (r-h-ṭ) — a small band of kinsmen

4.meaning: 'Mightier / dearer / more unassailable' — the comparative/superlative form meaning more powerful or more honoured than another.
4.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern ('more/most …'). The final -u is nominative, the form used when the word is a subject or predicate. The doubled zz reflects the root's two identical last letters merging in this pattern.
4.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, being unassailable and honoured

5.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
5.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
5.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'And you took/adopted Him (for yourselves)' — to take, seize, or adopt something, often for one's own purpose. The added t-stem gives the sense of taking for oneself.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb (a reflexive/middle 'iftaʿala' stem) with the connector 'and'. The suffix -tum marks 'you all' (more than one male) as the doer of the completed act; it is here lengthened to -tumū before the attached object pronoun -hu ('him/it'). The lengthening is part of this one suffix, not a separate piece.

9.meaning: 'Behind you / at your backs' — the area behind a person; figuratively, something cast aside, ignored, or put out of mind.
9.grammar: An adverb of place ('behind') with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, the form a word takes when it functions adverbially (telling where/when) or as an object. The suffix -kum means 'your' addressed to more than one male.
9.root: و-ر-ي / و-ر-أ (w-r-ʾ) — to be behind, beyond

10.meaning: 'Cast behind the back / treated as something forgotten' — neglected and disregarded, like a thing thrown behind one and ignored.
10.grammar: A noun/adjective formed from 'back' with the -iyy ending that turns a noun into a related descriptive form. The final -an is the indefinite accusative, the form used when a word is an object or describes the manner/state of an action.
10.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back; to appear, become outward

11.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
11.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

12.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
12.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

13.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
13.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

14.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
14.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

15.meaning: 'encompassing / all-encompassing' — one who surrounds a thing completely, encircling it so nothing escapes; figuratively, having total knowledge and control over it.
15.grammar: An active participle (a noun-like word naming the doer of an action: 'one who encompasses'). The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn ('n'-sound), marking it as indefinite ('an encompasser') and typically functioning as a subject or predicate.

1.meaning: 'And O my people!' — an affectionate call addressed to one's own community or kinsfolk.
1.grammar: A direct address: 'wa' ('and') plus the vocative particle 'yā' ('O') calling 'qawm' ('people'). The final -i stands in for the possessive 'my' (the 'ī' is shortened/dropped), so it means 'O my people'. 'qawm' is a collective term for one's community.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group / community

2.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'Do!', 'Act!', 'Work!' — an imperative urging people to carry out deeds or labor.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you'. The '-ū' ending is the plural-subject marker, so it commands more than one person: 'all of you, do/act'. The initial alif is a helping vowel to begin the word.
2.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work, to act; deeds

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: A noun meaning one's station, standing, rank, or status — the position or capacity a person occupies, whether literal place or figurative standing. With the attached 'your', it means 'your station' or 'your standing/way'.
4.grammar: A feminine noun ('station/standing/rank') in a possessive (iḍāfa) construction. Its tāʾ marbūṭa, normally pronounced '-a', surfaces as '-at-' when the word is in construct and carries a following possessor; the case vowel '-i' on it here is genitive (typical after a preposition or as a possessed noun). The suffix '-kum' is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' for a group.
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist; standing, station, status

5.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
5.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

6.meaning: Active participle meaning 'one who does/works', i.e. a doer, worker, or one engaged in action. Stated indefinitely, it means 'a worker' or 'one who acts'.
6.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' of the verb 'to work/do') used as a noun. The '-un' ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative state — typically the role of a subject or the thing being described.
6.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work, to act; deeds

7.meaning: A future-marking particle meaning 'shall / will (eventually)'. Placed before a present-tense verb, it pushes the action into the future, often with a sense of a more distant or assured 'in time, it shall come to pass'.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). Its sole function is to mark futurity on the present-tense verb that follows it.
7.root: — (particle; no root)

8.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
8.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

10.meaning: 'It comes to him / will come to him' — the act of arriving at or reaching a person, with an attached 'him' as the one reached.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he comes'). The attached -hi is the object 'him' (the -i vowel of this pronoun appears after an -i sound). The form is read as a sound (indicative/subjunctive) present rather than a command.
10.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring; to reach or befall.

11.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
11.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.
11.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

12.meaning: 'It disgraces him / will disgrace him' — to bring shame, humiliation, and abasement upon someone; an attached 'him' is the one disgraced.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form IV (the causative type — to 'bring' the state about). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). The attached -hi is the object 'him'. The weak final root letter shows as the long -ī before the pronoun.

13.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
13.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

14.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
14.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

15.meaning: 'A liar / one who lies' — an active participle naming the one who speaks falsehood, the doer of lying.
15.grammar: An active participle (the fāʿil 'doer' pattern) meaning 'one who lies'. The final -un (indefinite nominative) marks it as the subject or predicate — the form a word takes when naming the one who does the action or what something is.

16.meaning: 'And wait expectantly / keep watch' — a command to a group to watch and wait vigilantly for an outcome.
16.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the self-involving 'iftaʿala' stem, joined by 'and'. The -ū ending directs the order to more than one person ('you all'). The opening alif is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced when nothing precedes it.
16.root: ر-ق-ب (r-q-b) — to watch, observe, keep guard

17.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
17.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

18.meaning: An expression meaning 'with you' — combining the word for accompaniment, togetherness, or presence-alongside with the attached pronoun 'you' (a group). It signals being in the company of, or on the side of, the addressed people.
18.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment (maʿa, 'with/in the company of') carrying the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' for a group of males). It expresses togetherness or being alongside the people addressed.

19.meaning: 'A watcher / ever-watchful guardian' — one who observes and keeps close watch. The faʿīl pattern gives an intensive, constant sense (always watching).
19.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern. The final -un (indefinite nominative) marks it as a subject or predicate — the form used when naming the doer or what something is.
19.root: ر-ق-ب (r-q-b) — to watch, observe, keep guard

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

3.meaning: 'Our command / our decree / our affair / our matter' — a noun spanning an authoritative order, a divine decree, or simply a matter or affair, belonging to 'us'.
3.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -nā ('our'), showing possession. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used when the word is the subject of a sentence or otherwise the one performing/being identified.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'We delivered / rescued / brought to safety,' from a stem that intensifies the act of saving — to pull someone out of danger or peril and set them in security.
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb on the doubled-middle (faʿʿala) pattern, which adds force or causation: 'to save thoroughly, to rescue.' The -nā ending is the first-person plural subject, 'we,' marking a completed action already done.
4.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to be saved, to escape, deliverance

5.meaning: Shuʿayb — the proper name of a prophet sent to the people of Madyan.
5.grammar: A proper name (the diminutive form of a name) that is fully declinable (triptote). The -an ending marks the accusative case — fitting when the name is the one being sent or mentioned as object. The tanwīn here signals that the name belongs to the fully declinable class, not indefiniteness, since a proper name is inherently definite.

6.meaning: A connective phrase: 'and those who…' — the joining word 'and' attached to a masculine-plural relative pronoun that points to a group of people about whom something is then stated.
6.grammar: A particle of joining (wa, 'and') prefixed to a relative pronoun. 'Alladhīna' is masculine plural and indeclinable (its form does not change for case); it means 'those who / the ones who' and introduces a clause describing the group. The doubled 'w' reflects assimilation in pronunciation to a preceding word.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
7.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
7.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

8.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
8.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

9.meaning: With mercy / by mercy: tender compassion and active kindness that relieves and benefits. The noun names mercy as a quality and an outpouring of grace.
9.grammar: A feminine noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation — genitive because it follows a preposition, and the final -n marks it as indefinite ('a mercy').

10.meaning: 'From us' — the preposition 'from' fused with the pronoun 'us,' indicating source or origin in the first-person plural.
10.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / out of') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The nūn of 'min' assimilates into the following 'n', producing the doubled 'minnā.' It marks origin or source: 'from us / on our part.'

11.meaning: 'And it seized / took hold of' — to take, grip, or overtake forcefully; often used of a punishment or calamity overtaking people.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -at suffix marks a feminine singular doer of the completed action ('she/it seized'); its final vowel is here voiced as -ti to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster. The -a inside (akhadh-a) is the normal past-tense stem vowel.
11.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
13.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

14.meaning: The cry / the blast / the shout. It names a single mighty shout or thunderous sound — a sudden, overwhelming blast of noise.
14.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') plus a feminine noun (the -a/tāʾ marbūṭa marks it feminine and often a single instance, 'one cry'). The final -u ending marks the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing being named.

15.meaning: "And they came to be / and they became," from a verb that originally means "to enter upon the morning" and by extension "to end up in a certain state / to become." It describes a group transitioning into a new condition.
15.grammar: The "fa-" prefix means "so" or "and then," marking a result or sequence. The verb is in the completed (past) tense; the "-ū" ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). As one of the "sisters of kāna," this verb links a subject to a predicate state, hence "they became (something)."
15.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning / the coming of daybreak; by extension, to come to be in a state

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
16.root: — (particle)

17.meaning: Their homes or dwellings; the places where they live. 'Diyār' is the plural of 'dār,' a house, abode, or region one inhabits.
17.grammar: A plural noun followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive case, here triggered by the attached possessor and typical after prepositions or in possessive linkage ('the homes of…').

18.meaning: Fallen prone / lying lifeless — describing people collapsed motionless on their knees and faces, crouched and still as in death. A plural descriptive form.
18.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' form) describing those in a state of crouching motionless. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive — the form used for objects, or, as often here, for a descriptive 'state' word (telling how the subjects were: 'fallen prostrate').
18.root: ج-ث-م (j-th-m) — to crouch low and stay still; to lie collapsed/prone

1.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'as if / as though.' It introduces a comparison or likeness, treating a situation as resembling another — presenting something as if it were a certain way, whether or not it truly is.
1.grammar: A particle of comparison formed from 'ka-' ('like / as') joined to a particle meaning 'that.' Together they function as a single linking word, 'as if,' used to liken one circumstance to another. It is a particle, so it has no case ending of its own.

2.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
2.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

3.meaning: '(As though) they had never dwelt / thrived / lived in prosperity (there).' The root means to be free of need, to be self-sufficient and well-off, and to abide or flourish in a place. The subject is 'they.'
3.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix and a plural 'they' subject (the weak final root letter drops, leaving the -aw plural marker, with a silent spelling alif). The shortened form (no final -na) reflects that it follows a governing particle such as 'as if' or a negation, giving 'as though they had never thrived.'
3.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, well-off; to dwell in plenty

4.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
4.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

5.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
5.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

6.meaning: A being far off, remoteness, or removal — and as an exclamation, 'away (with them)!' or 'gone/perished be …', expressing dismissal and ruin.
6.grammar: A verbal noun in the indefinite accusative, shown by the -an ending. The accusative here typically signals an object, a state, or — as often with such words — an exclamation of curse or dismissal ('away with …!').
6.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be far, distant, or removed

7.meaning: 'To/for Madyan' — the proper name of the people and land of Midian, here introduced by a particle meaning 'to' or 'for'.
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to a proper name. Because it is a non-Arabic proper noun (a 'diptote'), it takes -a after the preposition instead of the usual -i, and it does not take the indefinite -n ending.
7.root: — (proper name)

8.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
8.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

9.meaning: 'It became far / remote' — to be or become distant; figuratively, to be removed from mercy, doomed, or cast away.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -at suffix marks a feminine singular doer of the completed action ('she/it became far'). The vowel pattern (with -i- in the middle) signals a state or quality coming about rather than a deliberate deed.
9.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — distance, remoteness, being far off

10.meaning: 'Thamūd' — the proper name of an ancient Arabian people to whom the prophet Ṣāliḥ was sent.
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -u is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being described. As a tribal proper name it is a 'diptote' and so does not take the indefinite -n ending.

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

3.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
3.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

4.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
4.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

5.meaning: 'And an authority / clear warrant' — sanctioned power, a compelling proof, or a mandate that gives one the right to act.
5.grammar: A noun joined by 'and'. The final -in is the indefinite genitive. Here the genitive case is inherited by coordination: the connector 'and' links this noun to a preceding genitive noun, so it takes the same case as the word it is joined to.
5.root: س-ل-ط (s-l-ṭ) — power, dominance, authority

6.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
6.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
6.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
1.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

2.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
2.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

3.meaning: 'And his chiefs / his notables' — the leading men, council, or elite of a people, joined to 'his'.
3.grammar: A collective noun ('the notables') with an attached possessive. The -i ending is genitive, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun. The suffix -hi means 'his'; its vowel is -i (rather than -hu) because it follows the genitive -i.
3.root: م-ل-أ (m-l-ʾ) — to fill; an assembly of leading men

4.meaning: 'But/so they followed' — to follow, obey, or go after someone; the added t-stem stresses pursuing or adhering closely.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb on the self-involving 'iftaʿala' stem, with the connector fa- ('so/then'). The -ū suffix marks 'they' (more than one male) as the doer of the completed action. The opening alif is a helping vowel for the initial cluster.
4.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

5.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or decree; can mean both 'an order given' and 'a state of affairs / business at hand,' depending on usage.
5.grammar: A noun. The final -a (fatḥa) is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into the accusative case.
5.root: أ-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; an affair or matter

6.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
6.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
7.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

8.meaning: 'Command, order, affair, matter.' This noun covers both a directive that is commanded and a situation or affair that comes to pass — what is decreed or what is the case.
8.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

9.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
9.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

10.meaning: 'Rightly-guided / sound / sensible' — leading to the right course; mature, well-directed and on a path of good judgement. The faʿīl pattern gives a settled, enduring quality.
10.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to an intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The final -in is the indefinite genitive, the form a noun takes after a preposition.
10.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgement, maturity

1.meaning: 'He goes ahead / leads the way' — to go in front of others as a leader so that they follow behind.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks 'he' as the doer, and the final -u is the indicative ending that marks an ongoing or habitual action. Built on a stem meaning to go before others as their leader.
1.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — to precede, go forward, come first

2.meaning: His people / his folk — the community, nation, or kinfolk belonging to him, with the attached pronoun marking possession.
2.grammar: A noun with the accusative -a ending, the form used when the word is a direct object, followed by the possessive suffix -hu ('his,' masculine singular).
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a group that stands together, a people

3.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
3.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
3.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

4.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
4.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

5.meaning: 'So/then he brought them down (to water)' — to lead a group down to a watering place; the verb's shape means to cause others to arrive at the water.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative 'afʿala' stem ('to make/cause to arrive at water'), with the connector fa- ('so/then'). The -a inside marks the completed action with 'he' as doer; the object suffix -hum ('them', more than one male) is voiced as -humu to ease the join with a following word.
5.root: و-ر-د (w-r-d) — to come to water, arrive at a watering place

6.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire as a blazing element, and by extension the well-known fire of punishment. The definite article makes it 'the Fire,' a specific, recognized fire rather than fire in general.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('the' + 'fire'), feminine. The article's lām assimilates into the following 'n' (shown by the doubling on nār). The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or the object of certain particles.
6.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, shine, illuminate (the noun nār, 'fire,' derives from this sense of light/blaze)

7.meaning: And how evil / wretched (it is)! — wa joined to biʾsa, a fixed verb of blame used to condemn something as bad, the opposite of niʿma ('how excellent'). It expresses strong disapproval.
7.grammar: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus biʾsa, a frozen verb of blame ('how wretched is …') that does not change for tense. It introduces strong condemnation of whatever follows as its subject, the counterpart of niʿma ('how good is …').
7.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — misery, hardship, wretchedness

8.meaning: A watering-place or drinking-place; the spot one arrives at to take water. By extension it can mean the act of coming down to water, or a daily portion/turn of water. The definite article 'the' is built in.
8.grammar: A definite singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case: it typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (as in 'X is …').
8.root: و-ر-د (w-r-d) — to come to water, arrive at a watering-place

9.meaning: Something or someplace that is come down to, approached, or arrived at — a passive description meaning 'that which is reached/visited (as one reaches water).' The definite article 'the' is built in.
9.grammar: A definite passive participle (the 'ma-…-ū-' pattern signals 'the one that is acted upon'). The final -u is the nominative case, typically marking a subject or a described thing; as a participle it commonly follows and describes a noun.
9.root: و-ر-د (w-r-d) — to come to water, arrive at a watering-place

1.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they were made to be followed / were pursued' — joining 'and' to a passive verb in which a group has something sent after or attached to them.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice on the causative (afʿala) pattern, prefixed with 'and' (wa). The internal vowelling (u–i) marks it passive: the subject does not act but has the action done to them ('they were followed / had [something] sent after them'). The -ū ending is the masculine plural subject, 'they.' The written final alif is silent.
1.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, pursue, come after

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: Feminine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'this (one)' — pointing to a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
3.grammar: A demonstrative ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand, contrasting with the masculine 'hādhā.' Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the form stays fixed whether subject, object, or after a preposition.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'a curse' — being placed far from mercy, an act of cursing or condemnation that drives one away from good and divine favor.

parts.en: accusative ending with nunation (the tā' is pronounced before it)

4.grammar: A feminine noun (its tā' marbūṭa sounded as 't' before the ending). The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (indefinite), the case typically used for a direct object or for an item closely specified by a verb ('…[were given] a curse').
4.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to drive far from mercy

5.meaning: And on the day (of) / and the day (of). The word for 'day' set as an adverb of time, joined by 'and'.
5.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the final -a, which here functions adverbially to mark a point in time ('on the day …'). The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
5.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a defined span of time

6.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
6.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

7.meaning: A fixed expression of strong blame meaning 'how evil/wretched it is!' or 'evil indeed is…'. It is a frozen verb of dispraise used to condemn whatever is mentioned after it.
7.grammar: A frozen verb of dispraise (its counterpart of praise is niʿma, 'how good'). It does not conjugate for tense; it introduces the thing being blamed and conveys 'what an evil … is …'.
7.root: ب-ء-س (b-ʾ-s) — misery, hardship, wretchedness

8.meaning: A gift, present, or aid given to someone — especially help or a bestowal granted as support. The definite article 'the' is built in.
8.grammar: A definite singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case, typically marking the word as a subject or the thing being identified (as in 'X is …').
8.root: ر-ف-د (r-f-d) — to aid, support, give a gift

9.meaning: Something given as a gift or grant — a passive description meaning 'that which is bestowed/presented.' The definite article 'the' is built in.
