12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
14.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

15.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
15.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

16.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

17.meaning: Means 'you (all) are given help / are supported and granted victory' — a present-tense passive verb: the help comes from another to the people addressed; they are the ones aided.
17.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The tu- prefix (with its vowel u) plus the -ūna ending means 'you (a group of males) are …ed' — the help is done TO you. The full -ūna ending marks it as a plain factual statement (indicative).

1.meaning: Means 'and keep up / duly perform and uphold' — a command from the form meaning 'to make stand'; used of establishing something properly and maintaining it (as with prayer), not merely starting it.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male, from the form aqāma ('to set up, establish'). The base command ends abruptly (aqim), but a connecting vowel -i is added here so it reads smoothly into the next word. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising; (form IV) establishing, upholding

2.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
2.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

3.meaning: Means 'the two ends / two edges / two extremities' — the dual of 'end' or 'extremity', naming exactly two outer limits or sides of something.
3.grammar: A dual noun (meaning exactly two). The stem ṭaraf means a single 'end / extremity'; the dual sense comes from the suffix. The -ay(i) ending is the dual form used in the genitive/accusative — the genitive being the case found after a preposition or when one noun is linked to a following noun ('the two ends OF …'). When the noun is joined to a following word, the dual's final -ni drops, leaving -ay(i).
3.root: ط-ر-ف (ṭ-r-f) — edge, extremity, end, outermost part

4.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
4.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the,' with its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the day') or as following a preposition or a particle that governs the genitive.

5.meaning: Means 'and during portions / drawing-near times' — the plural of a word for a part of the night close to the day, i.e. the early hours; the root conveys nearness and approach.
5.grammar: An indefinite plural noun. The final -an (nunation on a supporting alif) marks it indefinite and accusative — a case often used for nouns expressing time or circumstance ('during …'). The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
5.root: ز-ل-ف (z-l-f) — drawing near, nearness, a portion close by

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
7.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').
7.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, nightfall

8.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
8.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

9.meaning: Means 'the good deeds / virtuous acts' — the plural of 'a good thing'; specifically beautiful, beneficial actions and the good standing they earn.
9.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the …') marked by the prefix al- ('the'). The -āt ending is the regular feminine plural; its final vowel -i is the form this plural takes in the genitive or accusative — i.e. after a preposition, when linked to a following noun, or as the object of a verb.

10.meaning: They (feminine plural) drive away, take away, or cause to vanish — a verb expressing the action of making something depart or disappear, performed by a group of feminine subjects.
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the causative (Form IV) pattern, literally 'make to go.' The yu- prefix marks the third person and the causative voice ('cause to…'); on its own it does not fix the gender or number, and the -na ending here makes the subject feminine plural ('they,' for women or feminine nouns). Together: 'they (fem.) cause to go away.'

11.meaning: 'The evil deeds / bad actions' — plural of sayyi'a, a wrong or evil act, a misdeed or sin; the opposite of a good deed.
11.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the misdeeds'). The -i ending here is the case marker for the sound feminine plural in the genitive/accusative state, typically signalling that it follows a preposition, links to a preceding noun, or stands as an object.
11.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; misdeed, wrong

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: A reminder; a remembrance or admonition that brings truth to mind — the same notion as the previous word but without 'the,' so 'a reminding / as a reminder.'
13.grammar: A noun, 'reminder/admonition,' here indefinite ('a reminder'). The closing long -ā is a fixed feminine ending that does not inflect for case; the word's role in a sentence is shown by context rather than by a final case vowel.

14.meaning: For those who remember and call to mind — referring to people who keep something present in their awareness, especially those mindful and mentioning of Allah.
14.grammar: An active participle ('the remembering ones / mentioners') in the masculine plural, preceded by the preposition li- ('for, to') and the definite article al-. The -īna ending is the masculine plural in the object/oblique case, which is the form required after a preposition. So the whole means 'for the ones who remember.'

1.meaning: And be patient / endure steadfastly / persevere — sabr is the disciplined restraint of the self: bearing hardship calmly, holding firm, and not giving way to impatience or despair. The leading wa is the connective 'and.'
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person, 'be patient!', carrying the connective wa ('and'). The clipped, vowel-less ending is the normal shape of the singular command form.
1.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself, persevere

2.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
2.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'he lets go to waste / squanders / allows to be lost'. The core sense is causing something to be neglected, ruined, or forfeited rather than preserved.

parts.en: cause to be lost / let go to waste (stem)

5.grammar: An imperfect verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') and identifies the verb as belonging to a derived (augmented) form whose imperfect takes yu- rather than the ya- of the basic form; the meaning here is causative ('to cause to be lost'). The final -u ending marks the indicative mood — a plain statement.
5.root: ض-ي-ع (ḍ-y-ʿ) — to be lost, wasted, neglected

6.meaning: Means 'reward, wage, recompense'. The word denotes the due return for work or conduct — payment, compensation, or the reward earned by deeds.
6.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon, e.g. 'the reward' as what is given or not wasted) or the first term of a possessive pair when it is itself an object ('the reward of…').

7.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

7.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
7.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently

1.meaning: "So if not / then were it not for" — combines 'so/then' with 'lawlā', which introduces a 'were it not for…' condition (something whose absence would change the outcome) and can also urge 'why not…?'.

parts.en: were it not for / why not

1.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so, then', often marking a result) plus the particle 'lawlā'. As a conditional particle 'lawlā' sets up 'were it not for X (then Y would not be)'; as an incitement it means 'why do you not…?'. It is a function word, not inflected.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: The generations — successive ages or peoples who lived and passed away one after another; a community of people belonging to a particular era.
4.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the generations'), with the article al-. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition, marking the word as governed by something before it.
4.root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n) — joining together; an age or generation

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
6.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'

7.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
7.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
7.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

8.meaning: Possessors of a lasting remnant — those who retain an enduring portion of good sense, virtue, or sound judgment. The word names a remainder that persists, and in this usage it is read attributively (like 'people of a remnant'), so the remnant is one of moral integrity rather than a material leftover.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun, indefinite (no 'the'). The ending -tin combines the feminine -t with the indefinite genitive '-in' (nunation), placing 'a remnant' in the genitive case — typically after a preposition or linked as 'of' to a preceding word. By a well-attested classical reading it works attributively to mean those possessing a remaining portion of virtue or good sense (compare ūlū baqiyya, 'people of a remnant'), a nuance that has no single-word English equivalent.

9.meaning: They forbid, prohibit, or restrain — a verb describing a group who tell others to stop or hold back from something.
9.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya-…-na frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the ending -na shows they are the doers. The verb means 'to forbid' or 'to restrain (someone from something).'

10.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

11.meaning: The corruption — spoiling, ruin, wrongdoing, and the spreading of disorder; the opposite of putting things right or making them sound.
11.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the corruption') with the article al-. The final -i is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or linked by 'of' to a preceding noun.
11.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — corruption, spoiling, decay

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
13.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
15.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
15.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

16.meaning: 'than whoever / than the one who' — a fusion of the comparative preposition 'min' ('than, from') with the relative 'man' ('who/whoever'), introducing the person being compared to.
16.grammar: A contraction of the preposition 'min' ('than/from') and the relative-interrogative pronoun 'man' ('who'). The final 'n' of 'min' has merged into the 'm' of 'man' (shown by the doubling), so the two words are pronounced as one: 'mimman.' Both pieces are invariant particles with no case ending.

17.meaning: We delivered / we rescued. A verb meaning to bring someone to safety, saving them from danger or destruction. Carries the 'we' subject.
17.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb from the causative form, denoting a completed action. The suffix -nā marks the subject as first-person plural ('we'), indicating that the doers are 'we'.
17.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to be safe, escape; (causative) to deliver, rescue

18.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
18.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

19.meaning: And he followed / pursued — to follow closely, comply with, and take as one's guide or path, with deliberate adherence.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb in the form VIII pattern, which intensifies 'to follow' into following closely and submitting to. Prefixed with 'wa-' ('and') and bearing no subject ending, the bare form takes a third-person masculine singular subject ('he').
19.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, to pursue, to comply with

20.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
20.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

21.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
21.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

22.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
22.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

23.meaning: They were given ease and luxury — a verb describing people who were indulged with abundant comfort and affluence, often to the point of being spoiled by it.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice ('they were made to live in luxury'), Form IV. The u- vowelling marks the passive (something was done TO them), and the -ū ending is the masculine plural subject 'they.' So: 'they were given a life of ease.'

24.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
24.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

25.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
25.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
25.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

26.meaning: 'Criminals' / 'guilty ones' — those who commit grave sins or crimes, cutting themselves off from righteousness. It denotes wrongdoers steeped in sin and guilt.
26.grammar: An active participle (Form IV, 'one who commits crime/sin') in the masculine plural. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive form — the case used for an object or for a word describing a state ('as wrongdoers').
26.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or sin; guilt

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
3.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

4.meaning: So as to destroy or annihilate — a verb expressing the causing of ruin or perishing, framed as a purpose ('in order to destroy').
4.grammar: A present-tense causative (Form IV) verb meaning 'cause to perish,' preceded by purpose-li ('in order to'). This li forces the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). Together: 'so that he may destroy.'

5.meaning: 'the towns / settlements'. The plural of qarya, a town, village, or settled habitation — any gathered dwelling-place of people.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of qarya. It ends in a 'restricted' final long vowel written as alif maqṣūra (ى), which stays the same in all cases — its case is understood from context rather than shown by a changing vowel. The prefixed al- makes it definite ('the towns').
5.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather; a gathering-place, town/settlement

6.meaning: 'with wrongdoing / with injustice' — with putting things out of their right place: injustice, oppression, or wrong, governed by a preceding preposition.
6.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with') attached to the noun 'wrongdoing.' The ending -in is the genitive with indefinite 'nunation' ('with some wrong'); the genitive case is required after a preposition.
6.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, put out of place; darkness

7.meaning: While its/their people — 'and the people of it', i.e. the inhabitants or folk belonging to a place. 'Ahl' denotes the people of a household, town, or thing — those who belong to it.
7.grammar: A noun with the nominative case ending -u, marking it as a subject or the thing described (often opening a descriptive clause). The attached -hā is a feminine 'its/her', referring to a feminine or non-human possessor.
7.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, people, those who belong to something

8.meaning: 'Ones who set things right' — reformers, peacemakers, those who put matters in good order and mend what is broken. The active participle of the verb 'to set right'.
8.grammar: An active participle on the causative (Form IV) pattern, naming the doer: 'one who sets things right / a reformer'. The mu- prefix marks the doer, and the -ūna ending makes it masculine plural and nominative — the case for a subject or predicate ('they are reformers').

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
2.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

3.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
3.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

4.meaning: He certainly made or rendered — emphatically affirming that someone (Allah) did establish, appoint, or turn something into a particular state.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb ('he made') prefixed with emphatic la- ('surely, indeed'), which often answers a condition ('then he would surely have…'). The bare verb with final -a is third-person masculine singular ('he'). The verb 'jaʿala' means to make, to render something into a state, or to appoint.

5.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
5.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

6.meaning: "a community / a nation / a people" — a single group bound together as one body, typically by shared faith, way of life, or leadership; 'umma' is a collective people united around something.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun, indefinite ('a community'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain verbs of making/becoming; the final alif is the written seat of this ending.
6.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward, intend; a community/leadership (cf. imām)

7.meaning: One, single, sole — the feminine form of the word for 'one', denoting unity and singleness, that there is just one of something with no second alongside it.
7.grammar: A feminine singular adjective/numeral meaning 'one'. The taa marbuuta makes it agree with a feminine noun. The final -an (accusative, with tanwin) marks it as indefinite and as describing or counting an accusative noun. The opening wa- is a separate connecting particle ('and').
7.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — to be one, single, unique

8.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
8.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

9.meaning: They (will) cease / stop / leave off — used to express that some group keeps on doing something, since it normally appears in the negative ('they do not cease' = 'they keep on').
9.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending means 'they' (masculine plural); with this plural ending in place the prefix is read as plural 'they', not singular 'he'. The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood (a plain factual statement, not a command or a negated/subjunctive form). The verb 'to cease' very often pairs with a negation to mean 'continue / keep on'.

10.meaning: Ones differing or being at variance — people or things that diverge, disagree, and are diverse from one another.
10.grammar: An active participle (Form VIII, 'those who differ among themselves') in the masculine plural. The -īna ending is the masculine plural in the object/oblique case — the form used when the word is the object of a verb or governed by a preposition. Sense: 'differing ones, people at variance.'

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: He showed mercy, He had compassion — past-tense action of extending mercy and tender kindness.
3.grammar: A Form I past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, 'he had mercy.' The final -a is the standard ending marking a completed past action done by 'he.' The vowel pattern (a–i) is typical of verbs describing an inner state or quality such as mercy.

4.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
4.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

5.meaning: And for that, and for that very purpose — a connective phrase pointing back to a previously mentioned thing as the reason or aim.
5.grammar: A combination: wa ('and') + li- ('for, for the sake of') + the demonstrative dhālika ('that,' pointing to something distant or already mentioned). The li- expresses purpose or cause ('for that reason'). The form dhālika is the masculine singular 'that.'

6.meaning: He created them — a verb expressing the act of bringing a group into existence from nothing, with 'them' as the ones created.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb ('he created') with an attached object pronoun. The bare verb with -a is third-person masculine singular ('he'); the suffix -hum is the object 'them' (masculine plural). So: 'he created them.'

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and it was completed / fulfilled / came to its full measure'. The core sense is something reaching completion and perfection, being brought to its full and final state.
7.grammar: wa- is 'and'. tamma is a plain (Form I) past-tense verb, 'to be complete / fulfilled'. The suffix -t (a quiescent tā') marks a third-person singular feminine subject ('it / she'), agreeing with a feminine noun; the action is presented as completed.
7.root: ت-م-م (t-m-m) — completeness, fulfillment, perfection

8.meaning: The word, statement, or decree — an utterance or pronouncement; when ascribed to Allah, a binding decree or settled promise that is sure to be fulfilled.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun ('word, decree'). The ending -tu carries the feminine -t plus the nominative -u, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the word OF …').
8.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — speech, a word, an utterance

9.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
9.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

10.meaning: I shall certainly fill — an emphatic vow that the speaker will most assuredly fill something up completely.
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of strong vow. The la- prefix is the emphatic 'surely' that introduces an oath's answer, and the -anna at the end is the 'heavy' emphatic suffix that intensifies a promise or threat ('I will most certainly…'). The a- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). Together: 'I shall surely fill.'

11.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
11.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
11.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

12.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

13.meaning: The jinn — a created order of unseen beings made of smokeless fire, hidden from human sight and morally accountable like humankind.
13.grammar: A definite collective noun naming the unseen beings (the jinn). The -ti ending carries the feminine/collective -t plus the genitive -i, marking the word as following a preposition or linked by 'of' to a preceding noun.

14.meaning: And mankind / the people — humankind, people in general. The Arabic noun is collective, denoting humanity as a body.
14.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and'; 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', written al-nās, said an-nās). A collective noun for people. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF …').
14.root: أ-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — sociability, familiarity, being human (a minority view traces it to ن-و-س, n-w-s)

15.meaning: All together / one and all — an emphatic word meaning the entirety of a group, every last one without exception.
15.grammar: An emphatic plural used to stress totality ('all of them, every one'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, agreeing with a plural noun it reinforces.

1.meaning: 'And all / each one' — referring comprehensively to every member of a group, 'each and every.'
1.grammar: 'And' + the totality-word kull ('all/each'). The '-an' (nunation) is the accusative indefinite ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). Standing alone with nunation, kull means 'each one / all of them.'

2.meaning: We narrate, recount, or relate — a verb describing the telling of a story or account in sequence, with 'we' as the tellers.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb ('we relate'). The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -u is the indicative mood, the plain 'this is happening / is done' form used when no particle changes the ending. Sense: to recount a narrative in order.
2.root: ق-ص-ص (q-ṣ-ṣ) — following a track; narrating, recounting

3.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: Tidings / reports / accounts — the plural of an item of significant news, especially weighty information about important events or matters.
5.grammar: An irregular (broken) plural meaning 'tidings / pieces of news'. The final -i is the genitive ending, typically appearing after a preposition or when linked to a following noun in a possessive chain ('… news of …').
5.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, momentous report

6.meaning: 'the messengers' — the envoys sent by Allah, taken definitely as a known group.
6.grammar: The prefix al- ('the') makes it definite (its 'l' assimilates to the following 'r'). The base is the broken plural of rasūl. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the messengers') or follows a preposition.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: We make firm, steady, and steadfast — a verb describing the act of strengthening, confirming, or giving stability to something, with 'we' as the doers.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern, 'to make firmly steadfast.' The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we') in a causative/intensive verb. The final -u is the indicative mood (the plain ongoing form). Sense: to render firm and steady.

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

10.meaning: Your heart — the inner core of a person as the seat of feeling, courage, and understanding; addressed to a single male 'you.'
10.grammar: A noun ('heart') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending before the pronoun is the accusative, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb ('… the heart'). The suffix -ka means 'your,' addressing one male. So: 'your heart' as a grammatical object.
10.root: ف-ء-د (f-ʾ-d) — the heart; being deeply stirred

11.meaning: And there came to you — a verb stating that something arrived or reached a single male addressee, joined to the preceding by 'and.'
11.grammar: A past-tense verb ('came') joined by wa ('and') and carrying an attached object pronoun. The bare verb is third-person masculine singular ('he/it came'); the suffix -ka is the object 'you' (one male). So: 'and it came to you.'
11.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — coming, arriving

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
13.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

14.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
14.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
14.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

15.meaning: And an admonition or exhortation — a heartfelt warning and counsel meant to soften, caution, and turn one toward the good.
15.grammar: A feminine singular verbal noun ('an admonition'), indefinite (no 'the'), joined by wa ('and'). The ending -tun combines the feminine -t with the indefinite nominative '-un' (nunation), typically marking the word as a subject or as a thing being introduced ('and there is an admonition').

16.meaning: And a reminder — something that brings a truth back to mind and rouses awareness; a means of remembrance and heedfulness.
16.grammar: A feminine verbal noun ('a reminder'), joined by wa ('and'). It ends in the fixed long vowel -ā (written as alif maqṣūra), a form that does not change for case — so it stays the same whether subject, object, or after a preposition.
16.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, mentioning, reminding

17.meaning: A combination meaning 'for the believers' — 'to/for' + 'the' + 'those who have faith': people characterized by belief, trust, and security in faith.
17.grammar: The prefix li- is the preposition 'for/to'; 'al-' ('the') follows, its alif elided after li-. 'mu'minīn' is the active participle 'believers' (the mu- prefix forms the doer: 'those who have faith'). The -īna ending is the masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (versus -ūna for the subject case), here governed by the preposition 'for'.

1.meaning: And say — a command to one person to utter or speak words. The plain, central act of speaking aloud.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male, 'say!' from a hollow verb (middle root letter 'w' drops out in the command). The vowel-less ending is the standard singular masculine imperative. Prefixed wa- 'and' joins it to a preceding clause.

2.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

5.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'Do!', 'Act!', 'Work!' — an imperative urging people to carry out deeds or labor.
5.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you'. The '-ū' ending is the plural-subject marker, so it commands more than one person: 'all of you, do/act'. The initial alif is a helping vowel to begin the word.
5.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work, to act; deeds

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

7.meaning: A noun meaning one's station, standing, rank, or status — the position or capacity a person occupies, whether literal place or figurative standing. With the attached 'your', it means 'your station' or 'your standing/way'.
7.grammar: A feminine noun ('station/standing/rank') in a possessive (iḍāfa) construction. Its tāʾ marbūṭa, normally pronounced '-a', surfaces as '-at-' when the word is in construct and carries a following possessor; the case vowel '-i' on it here is genitive (typical after a preposition or as a possessed noun). The suffix '-kum' is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' for a group.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist; standing, station, status

8.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
8.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

9.meaning: Ones who work, act, or do — people engaged in deeds and activity; those who carry out and perform.
9.grammar: An active participle ('working ones, doers') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending is the masculine plural in the subject (nominative) case, the form used when the word is the doer or subject ('they are workers / they are acting').

1.meaning: And wait, watch, or expect — a command to a group to await an outcome, often with the sense of watching for what is to come.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group, joined by wa ('and'), in the Form VIII pattern meaning 'to wait, await, watch for.' The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'). So: 'and wait, all of you.'

2.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
2.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

3.meaning: Ones who wait / those who watch and expect — people in a state of awaiting or anticipating something. As a participle it names the doers of waiting.
3.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural. The -ūna ending marks the plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence, as opposed to the object form -īna. Built on a reflexive/intensive pattern, it means 'those engaged in awaiting.'

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: The unseen — all that is hidden from the senses and lies beyond human perception, known fully only to Allah.
2.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'that which is hidden, the unseen.' The final -u is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the unseen OF …').

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

5.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
5.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

6.meaning: It is brought back / it is returned. A passive verb meaning that something is made to go back or is sent back to a point of origin or destination. The doer of the action is left unnamed; the focus is on the thing that undergoes the return. Often used of all affairs and creatures being made to return to their ultimate source.

parts.en: he/it (present-tense subject marker, here vowelled for the passive)
is returned / is brought back (passive stem)

6.grammar: A present-tense passive verb in the third person masculine singular ('he/it'). The yu- prefix marks an ongoing or future action with an 'it' subject, and the internal u-a vowel pattern (yuC-CaCu) signals the passive voice: the subject does not act but is acted upon ('is returned' rather than 'returns'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, the plain, unmarked form a verb takes when simply stating that something happens.
6.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, to go back, to come back

7.meaning: The matter, affair, or command; a thing decided upon or ordered, or a situation/business at hand. It can denote both a "command" and an "affair" depending on usage.
7.grammar: A definite noun with prefixed al- ("the"). The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as the thing an action is predicated of.
7.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; matter, affair

8.meaning: The whole of it, the entirety of it, every part of it taken together. It combines the noun for 'totality/wholeness' with an attached pronoun referring back to something already mentioned, asserting that the matter applies completely and without exception.
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/whole' carrying the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks the word as a subject or the thing being described. The attached -hu is a possessive/referential pronoun meaning 'it' or 'his', so the whole means 'all of it'. As a third-person masculine singular pronoun it points back to a previously named thing.

9.meaning: So worship Him / then serve Him. A command addressed to a single person to direct worship, humble service, and devoted obedience toward Him. The verb conveys total submission and reverent servitude offered to the one addressed by the attached 'Him'.

parts.en: so / then (connecting particle drawing a conclusion)

9.grammar: A command (imperative) directed at one male person ('you, worship!'), built on the bare verb stem with no person prefix, which is how Arabic forms a direct order. The form rests on its stem with no mood vowel, the natural shape of a command. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it', telling whom the action falls upon. The leading fa- means 'so' or 'then', linking the command to what came before as its natural consequence; the helping vowel under the initial alif (heard as 'u') is only there to ease pronunciation after the fa- is joined.
9.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, to submit in devotion

10.meaning: And rely / and place your trust. A command (singular 'you') to entrust one's affairs fully to another and depend on Him completely, with calm reliance.
10.grammar: A masculine-singular command (imperative) addressed to one person: 'you, rely!'. It comes from a Form V verb pattern (tafaʿʿala) that conveys taking something fully upon oneself — here, deliberately committing one's reliance to another. The vowel-less ending (sukūn) is the normal final state of an imperative.
10.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, reliance, appointing someone to manage one's affairs

11.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
11.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
13.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

14.meaning: 'With/being heedless' — the preposition/particle 'bi' attached to 'ghāfil', one who is unaware, inattentive, or neglectful, failing to take notice.
14.grammar: The particle 'bi-' governs the following word into the genitive case. 'Ghāfil' is an active participle ('one who is heedless'). The '-in' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive; the 'bi-' here commonly adds emphasis within a negation ('not at all heedless').

15.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
15.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

16.meaning: You (plural) do, make, work, or act. A present/future verb addressed to a group, covering deeds and actions in general — what people carry out and put into practice.
16.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'); the -ūna ending makes it masculine plural ('you all') and signals the indicative mood — the ordinary statement-form used for actions that are happening or will happen. Within -ūna the long ū (wāw) carries the plurality and the final n (nūn) marks the indicative.
16.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act
